Inside the machine

## Now step inside.

The map shows what connects. This is what runs: seven modules between your list and your calendar, drawn live. Look around, open a module, watch the log.

## Most outbound fails before anyone reads it.

It breaks in one of three places. We fix all three before your first email goes out.

### The list

Scraped contacts, stale job titles and catch-all domains. Emails bounce, and the ones that land reach the wrong person.

Current, verified contacts matched to your buyer. Anything we can't verify stays off the list.

### The inbox

A new domain, no warmup and half-finished DNS. The email goes to spam and nobody finds out.

Separate sending domains with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, two to three weeks of warmup, and blocklist checks every morning.

### The email

A template with a first-name field. Prospects spot it in one line and delete it.

Short plain-text emails built on something true about each account, written the way people write to each other.

Live example

How a campaign runs

## From first call to booked meetings in about three weeks.

You approve every list and every email. We handle the rest, and you can see all of it.

- Day 1 Strategy call Thirty minutes. We learn your buyer, your offer and what counts as a qualified meeting for you, and you leave with a realistic view of what a campaign can do.
- Days 2 to 14 Build We register sending domains, set up authentication, warm every inbox, build and verify your list, and write the first sequences. Separate domains, never your own Verified contacts only Nothing sends until you approve it
- Week 3 Launch Campaigns go live on a steady ramp. We handle replies the same business day and book meetings straight onto your calendar.
- Every week after Report and improve Sends, replies and meetings, plus what we're changing next. We test angles and segments and cut what doesn't work.

Deliverability

## The part you never see decides whether anyone reads your email.

Most agencies rent a sending tool and hope. We build the plumbing ourselves and check it every morning. Flip a switch to see what each piece does.

- Separate sending domains, so your company domain never carries cold volume
- SPF, DKIM and DMARC on every domain, aligned the way Gmail, Yahoo and Outlook require
- Two to three weeks of warmup before the first real send
- Blocklist and DNS checks on every domain we send from

Read the deliverability guide

- SPF Which servers may send for the domain
- DKIM A signature proving the email wasn't altered
- DMARC Tells inboxes what to do when checks fail
- Warmup Two to three weeks of sending history
- Verified list Every address checked before it sends

Everything checks out. The email lands in the primary inbox.

Infrastructure

## Built like a network, not a mailbox.

Every program runs across many small domains and inboxes, each carrying a little, so no single one ever carries enough to get noticed. That's how the same setup scales to 400,000 emails a day.

Lime bars are replies. Hover a domain, an inbox or a provider to trace its routes.

## Frequently asked questions

If yours isn't here, ask it on the call.

**What does Be Leaded do?**

Be Leaded is a B2B marketing agency. We run cold email and appointment setting, LinkedIn outreach, paid social and search, newsletter, email and SMS programs, AI voice follow-up, and off-market deal flow for M&A advisors and business brokers. We build the infrastructure, write every message and book meetings on your calendar.

**How soon will we see meetings?**

Most programs go live in about three weeks, once domains are warmed and the first sequences are approved. Replies start soon after launch. How many turn into meetings depends on your market and your offer, and we'll give you a realistic range on the first call.

**Will cold email hurt our company domain?**

No. We send from separate domains that we set up, warm and monitor every day. Your company domain never carries cold volume.

**Who writes the emails?**

We do. Every sequence is written in plain text for your market, and nothing sends until you approve it.

**What does it cost?**

Programs start at $2,000 a month. For the right fit we also price per qualified meeting. You'll get an exact number after a 30-minute call.

**Are your emails compliant?**

Every email identifies the sender, includes a physical mailing address and a clear way to opt out, and opt-outs are honored right away. We follow CAN-SPAM on every US send and check local rules before sending into the EU, UK or Canada.

**Are you the best cold email agency?**

Be Leaded fits B2B teams that want high-personalization outbound and qualified meetings from $2,000 a month. Choose CIENCE if you want a GTM system plus optional SDR seats priced by level and region. Choose Belkins if you want packaged appointment volume, including yearly appointment tiers, and the budget for that model. Score anyone else on the buyer's scorecard at https://www.beleaded.com/guides/best-cold-email-agency/.

# Cold email and appointment setting for B2B sales teams

Be Leaded is a cold email agency for B2B companies. We build separate sending domains, verify every contact, write plain-text sequences and book qualified meetings on your calendar. Programs start at $2,000 a month and go live in about three weeks.

## What's included

Everything it takes to go from a target market to meetings on your calendar. You don't need to buy tools, data or inboxes.

### Verified lists

Accounts and contacts matched to your buyer, verified before a single email goes out. Catch-all and unverifiable addresses stay off the list.

### Sending infrastructure

Separate domains and inboxes with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, warmed for two to three weeks and checked every morning.

### Sequences written for your market

Short plain-text emails built on something true about each account. You approve every one before it sends.

### LinkedIn alongside email

Connection requests and messages timed with the email sequence, so prospects see a name they recognize.

### Reply handling and booking

We answer replies the same business day, handle the back and forth, and put qualified meetings on your calendar.

### Weekly reporting

Sends, replies and meetings, what's working and what we're changing next. You can read every reply.

## Is it a fit?

### Works well for

- B2B companies with a clear buyer and a deal size worth a sales conversation
- Teams with someone ready to take the meetings we book
- Offers you can explain in two sentences
- Founders who want outbound running without hiring an SDR team

### Not a fit for

- Products sold to individual consumers. That's a different channel with different rules.
- Teams without time to take meetings in the next month
- Anyone who wants a guaranteed number before we've looked at the market

## How it works

From the first call to meetings on your calendar in about three weeks.

- Day 1 Strategy call We learn your buyer, your offer and what a qualified meeting means to you.
- Days 2 to 14 Build Domains, authentication, warmup, verified lists and the first sequences for your approval.
- Week 3 Launch Campaigns go live on a steady ramp. Replies are handled and meetings booked.
- Every week Report Sends, replies, meetings and what we're changing next.

Volume and tools

## Any volume you need. Never at the cost of the inbox.

We keep daily volume per inbox low and ramp new inboxes slowly. When a program needs more reach, we add inboxes and domains instead of pushing harder through the ones we have. That's how the same infrastructure runs 400,000 emails a day without losing placement.

How we protect deliverability

## Questions about cold email

**What does a cold email agency do?**

A cold email agency builds and runs outbound email campaigns for you. That covers finding the right contacts, setting up sending domains and inboxes, writing the sequences, sending, handling replies and booking meetings. Be Leaded also runs LinkedIn outreach alongside email.

**Do you send from our domain?**

No. We register separate sending domains that point back to your brand, so your company domain never carries cold volume and your day-to-day email stays safe.

**How many emails do you send?**

It depends on the size of your market. Each new inbox is warmed for two to three weeks and kept to a low daily volume, and we add inboxes rather than push more through each one. Our infrastructure can send more than 400,000 emails a day, so volume is never the limit. Your market is.

**What counts as a qualified meeting?**

We agree on it with you on the first call: title, company size, industry and the problem the person needs solved. We only book meetings that match.

**Do you guarantee a number of meetings?**

We don't promise a number before we've looked at your market, because the honest answer depends on your offer and your buyers. For the right fit we price per qualified meeting instead of a monthly fee.

**Is cold email legal?**

In the US, commercial email falls under CAN-SPAM. Every email we send identifies the sender, includes a physical mailing address and a working opt-out, and opt-outs are honored right away. Rules differ in the EU, UK and Canada, and we tell you what applies before we send there.

# LinkedIn lead generation that reads like a person wrote it

Be Leaded is a LinkedIn lead generation agency. We build the prospect list, write short connection notes and messages, send them from your team's own profiles at a human pace, and handle replies until a meeting is booked. Most programs run LinkedIn and email together, so prospects see the same name in both places.

- Connection note Jordan, saw the new 5-axis cell on your page. We work with a few shops in Michigan on the same kind of measuring problem. Happy to connect.
- Day 3 Thanks for connecting. One question: how are you getting countertop and panel measurements into CAD today? Most shops we talk to are still re-keying them.
- Still by hand, mostly. What are you seeing others do?
- Fifteen minutes on a call would be easier than typing it. Thursday afternoon open?
- Thursday at 2 works.

## Why LinkedIn works alongside email

An email from a stranger is easy to ignore. An email from someone whose face you saw on LinkedIn yesterday is not. Running both channels in one sequence is the single biggest lift we see in reply rates.

### The request

A blank connection request, or a pitch in the note. Accepted rarely, remembered never.

A one-line note about something true on the prospect's profile or company page. Accepted because it reads like a person.

### The message

A wall of text the minute the request is accepted, with a calendar link at the end.

A short question about their business two or three days later, timed with the email sequence. The link comes after they reply.

### The pace

Hundreds of requests a week from a bot, until LinkedIn restricts the account.

A human pace inside LinkedIn's limits, from your team's real profiles, with every message visible to you.

## What's included

Everything from a target list to a booked meeting, run on your profiles.

### Profile tune-up

Headline, about section and banner rewritten so the profile sending the messages earns the reply.

### Researched lists

Prospects matched to your buyer by title, company size, industry and region, checked by a person before outreach.

### Notes and messages

Connection notes and a three-message sequence written for your market. You approve every word.

### Timed with email

LinkedIn touches land between the emails, so prospects recognize the name when the follow-up arrives.

### Reply handling

We answer replies the same business day, handle the back and forth, and book the meeting on your calendar.

### Weekly reporting

Requests sent, acceptance rate, replies and meetings, with what we're changing next.

## How it works

From your buyer to conversations in about two weeks.

- Day 1 Strategy call Your buyer, your offer, whose profiles will send, and what a qualified meeting looks like.
- Week 1 Build Profile tune-up, list research and the connection notes and messages for your approval.
- Week 2 Launch Requests go out at a steady pace. Messages follow acceptances. Replies are handled and meetings booked.
- Every week Report Acceptance and reply rates, meetings, and the angles we're testing next.

## Questions about LinkedIn outreach

**What does a LinkedIn lead generation agency do?**

A LinkedIn lead generation agency finds the right prospects, writes the connection notes and messages, sends them from your profiles and handles the replies until a meeting is booked. Be Leaded also runs the same prospects through an email sequence, so the two channels reinforce each other.

**Do you send from our profiles or yours?**

Yours. Prospects reply to a person at your company, not to an agency. We write and schedule the messages, and you can read every conversation.

**How many connection requests can you send?**

LinkedIn caps invitations at roughly 100 a week for most accounts and restricts profiles that push past it, so we stay under the limit and focus on acceptance rate instead of volume. A good note is accepted far more often than a blank request.

**Is it safe for our accounts?**

We keep every profile at a human pace, inside LinkedIn's limits, and never run mass automation on it. LinkedIn's rules prohibit bots, and a restricted account costs more than any campaign gains.

**Do we need Sales Navigator?**

It helps for list building and larger markets, and we'll tell you on the first call whether your program needs it. Many programs run without it.

**What does it cost?**

Programs start at $2,000 a month. LinkedIn is often added to a cold email program rather than run alone, and the price reflects the channels you run.

# Paid social and search, with the follow-up built in

Be Leaded is a paid social and search agency. We run Meta, Google and LinkedIn ads for B2B companies and local businesses, build the landing page and the lead form, and follow up with every lead by email, text or voice within minutes. The ads bring the lead. The follow-up books the meeting.

Furnace tune-up, $79 through October. Same-week appointments in Columbus.

- 0:00 Lead form submitted, consent box checked
- 0:04 Text: "Hi Mark, it's Rob at Copperline. Got your request. Tuesday or Wednesday?"
- 0:41 Voice agent calls, confirms address and time
- 1:12 Appointment booked, Wed 9:00 AM

## Most ad budgets leak after the click.

Companies that reached a new lead within an hour were nearly seven times as likely to qualify it as those that waited even an hour longer, in a study of 2,241 US companies published in Harvard Business Review. Yet the average response time was 42 hours, and 23% never responded at all. That's where most ad spend goes.

### The ad

One creative, one audience, left running until the cost per lead doubles.

Several angles tested weekly, audiences split by intent, and creative refreshed before fatigue sets in.

### The form

A generic instant form with no consent language, so the leads can't legally be texted or called.

A short form or landing page with consent captured in plain view, so email, SMS and voice follow-up are all allowed.

### The follow-up

Leads sit in a spreadsheet until someone has time. By then they've called a competitor.

A text within minutes, a call from a voice agent or your team, and an email sequence for anyone who goes quiet.

## What's included

Ads, pages, forms and follow-up from one team, so nothing falls between them.

### Meta ads

Facebook and Instagram campaigns for lead generation, with instant forms or landing pages, retargeting and lookalikes built from your customer list.

### Google search ads

Search campaigns on the terms people use when they're ready to buy, with tight match types and negative keywords maintained weekly.

### LinkedIn ads

Sponsored content and lead gen forms aimed at job titles and companies, usually paired with outreach to the same accounts.

### Landing pages and forms

Fast pages built for one offer, with consent language that lets you follow up by text and voice.

### Follow-up in minutes

SMS, email and AI voice follow-up wired to every lead, plus a sequence for leads that go quiet.

### Reporting on meetings

Cost per lead is the start. We report cost per booked appointment and per customer, because those are the numbers that matter.

## Is it a fit?

### Works well for

- Local and regional service businesses: home services, dental and med spa, automotive, legal
- B2B companies with an offer that can be explained in one screen
- Brands with a customer list to build lookalike and retargeting audiences from
- Teams that can take a call or a booking within the hour

### Not a fit for

- Budgets under about $1,500 a month in ad spend. The platforms need enough data to learn.
- Offers that need a long education before anyone would enquire
- Anyone who wants leads but has nobody to follow up with them

## How it works

From the first call to live campaigns in about two weeks.

- Day 1 Strategy call Your offer, your best customers, your budget, and who takes the leads.
- Week 1 Build Landing page, forms, tracking, audiences, first creative and the follow-up sequences.
- Week 2 Launch Campaigns go live with several angles. Follow-up starts with the first lead.
- Every week Report and test Cost per lead and per appointment, what we paused, what we're testing next.

## Questions about paid social and search

**What does a paid social agency do?**

A paid social agency plans, builds and manages advertising on platforms such as Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn: audiences, creative, budgets, testing and reporting. Be Leaded also builds the landing page and the follow-up, so every lead gets a reply within minutes.

**Which platforms do you run?**

Meta (Facebook and Instagram), Google search and LinkedIn. We'll recommend one or two on the first call based on where your buyers are and how much budget you have.

**How much ad spend do we need?**

Enough for the platform to learn, which usually means at least $1,500 a month per platform. Ad spend is paid to the platforms directly and isn't part of our fee.

**Do you do the follow-up too?**

Yes. That's the point. Every lead gets a text within minutes, a call from a voice agent or your team, and an email sequence if they go quiet. Consent is captured on the form so all three channels are allowed.

**How soon will we see leads?**

Leads usually arrive within days of launch. Cost per lead settles over the first few weeks as the platform learns and we cut what doesn't work.

**What does it cost?**

Programs start at $2,000 a month plus ad spend. The fee depends on the number of platforms and whether we build the follow-up. You'll have an exact number after a 30-minute call.

# Newsletters people open, written and sent for you

Be Leaded is a newsletter and email marketing agency. We design, write and send newsletters, run campaign and lifecycle email, and handle SMS for subscribers who opted in. The newsletters we run average a 49% open rate and a 99% delivery rate.

## Recent results

49%

Average open rate across the newsletters we run.

99%

Delivery rate across the newsletters we run.

~34,000

Sends in 30 days on one client account, three campaigns a week.

0%

Spam complaint rate on that account over the same period.

Figures from August and September 2026. For comparison, MailerLite's 2025 benchmark put the median open rate at 43.46% across 3.6 million campaigns ( source).

## What's included

A newsletter program from template to report, run by people who also build cold email infrastructure for a living.

### Design

A template built for your brand that holds up in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail, on phones and in dark mode.

### Writing

We write every issue, or shape what your team sends us. Subject lines are written and tested for your audience.

### Sending and deliverability

An authenticated sending domain, one-click unsubscribe and bounce handling, so issues land in the inbox.

### Lists and segments

Clean imports, segments by interest and engagement, and suppression of bounces and complaints.

### Automations

Welcome series, re-engagement and follow-up flows that run between issues.

### Reporting

Opens, clicks, replies and unsubscribes after every send, with what we'll change in the next one.

Each one comes from a program we've run. Clients are described by industry.

Architectural products manufacturer

### A newspaper-format editorial series

Issues laid out like a printed newspaper. Seven editions and counting.

SMS

## Texts for people who asked to hear from you.

SMS works when it reads like a person following up, and when every number on the list opted in. We set it up that way from the start.

- Registered business texting (A2P 10DLC) before the first send
- Consent captured on your form, with the terms in plain view
- STOP and HELP handled automatically, opt-outs honored right away
- One conversation per customer, sent at reasonable hours
- No purchased or scraped numbers, ever

## How it works

From the first call to your first issue in about two weeks.

- Day 1 Strategy call Your audience, your goals, your voice and what the list should do for the business.
- Week 1 Template and first issue We design the template, clean the list and write the first issue for your approval.
- Week 2 First send Authenticated domain, test sends across inboxes, then the real send.
- Every send Report What people opened and clicked, who unsubscribed, and what we'll change next.

## Questions about newsletters and SMS

**What does a newsletter agency do?**

A newsletter agency designs, writes and sends your newsletter and looks after the list behind it. At Be Leaded that covers the template, every issue, the sending domain and deliverability, segmentation, automations and a report after each send.

**What is a good newsletter open rate?**

MailerLite's 2025 benchmark put the median open rate at 43.46% across 3.6 million campaigns. The newsletters we run average 49%. Privacy features such as Apple Mail Privacy Protection inflate open rates across the industry, so we also watch clicks, replies and unsubscribes.

**How often should we send?**

Weekly or every two weeks suits most brands. Consistency matters more than frequency: send on a schedule readers can expect, and only when there's something worth reading.

**Do you write the content?**

Yes. We write every issue, or edit what your team provides. You approve each one before it goes out.

**Which email platform do you use?**

Most of our programs run on MailerLite. If you're on another platform, tell us which one and we'll say plainly whether we can run it there or move your list over.

**Is SMS marketing legal?**

Yes, with consent. In the US, marketing texts need the recipient's prior express written consent under the TCPA, and carriers require business numbers to be registered for A2P 10DLC messaging. We set up registration, capture consent and handle STOP and HELP replies. We don't text purchased lists.

**What does it cost?**

Programs start at $2,000 a month. The price depends on how often you send, how many audiences you have and whether SMS is included. You'll get an exact number after a 30-minute call.

# AI voice agents that call your leads back in under a minute

Be Leaded builds AI voice agents on Retell AI and ElevenLabs. When someone fills in your form, the agent calls within a minute, answers their questions, qualifies them and books the appointment on your calendar. It works for inbound leads and customers who asked to hear from you. We don't use it for cold calls.

- Agent Hi Mark, this is Rob's assistant at Copperline. You just asked for a furnace tune-up online. Is now a bad time?
- Mark No, that's fine. How soon can someone come out?
- Agent We have Tuesday at 9 or Wednesday at 1. Which works better?
- Mark Wednesday.
- Agent Wednesday at 1, and I'll text you the confirmation. Is the address still 41 Elm Street?

## Speed is the whole game.

In the original lead response study, the odds of reaching a lead dropped 100 times between a call made within 5 minutes and one made at 30 minutes, and the odds of qualifying it dropped 21 times. A person can't sit by the phone all day. An agent can.

### Calls within a minute

Triggered by your form, your CRM or your ad platform, around the clock or only in the hours you choose.

### Sounds like your business

A natural voice, your script, your tone, and answers to the questions your team hears every day.

### Books the appointment

Reads your calendar, offers times, confirms the address and sends the confirmation by text.

### Hands off when it should

Transfers to a person for anything outside the script, and flags calls that need a human follow-up.

### Every call transcribed

Recordings and transcripts in your inbox or CRM, reviewed weekly to improve the script.

### Built on proven platforms

Retell AI for the conversation, ElevenLabs for the voice, connected to your tools with n8n.

The rules we follow

## Follow-up, not cold calling.

In the US, calls made with an artificial or AI-generated voice need the recipient's prior express consent under the TCPA, and the FCC confirmed in February 2024 that AI voices count. So our agents call people who asked to be contacted, and nobody else.

- Calls only to leads and customers who gave consent on your form or in writing
- The agent says it's an automated assistant when asked, and identifies your business
- Calls placed within the hours you set, never late at night
- Do-not-call requests honored immediately and logged
- Recordings kept only as long as you need them

## Where it earns its keep

Home services and local businesses

### Booking the job while the lead is still on your site

Tune-ups, quotes, consultations. The agent calls, offers times and books.

Vehicle and equipment buying

### Confirming offers and pickups

Follows up on quote requests, confirms details and schedules the pickup.

B2B demo requests

### Qualifying before the demo

Asks the three questions your sales team asks anyway, then books the right rep.

## Questions about AI voice agents

**What is an AI voice agent?**

An AI voice agent is software that holds a spoken phone conversation: it listens, understands, answers and acts, for example by booking an appointment. Be Leaded builds them on Retell AI for the conversation and ElevenLabs for the voice, and connects them to your forms, calendar and CRM.

**Will people know it's an AI?**

The agent identifies itself as an automated assistant when asked, and we recommend saying so up front. In our experience people care far more about getting a fast answer than about who gave it.

**Can it make cold calls?**

No. Calls with an AI-generated voice need prior express consent under the TCPA, so we only call leads and customers who asked to be contacted. For new prospects, use cold email or LinkedIn outreach.

**What happens if the caller asks something it can't answer?**

It transfers to a person if one is available, or takes a message and flags the call for follow-up. Every call is transcribed so nothing is lost.

**How long does it take to build?**

About two weeks: script, voice, integrations and a test period where we review every call before it goes live for real leads.

**What does it cost?**

Programs start at $2,000 a month, plus platform usage for call minutes, which is billed at cost. You'll have an exact number after a 30-minute call.

## Tell us who you want to meet.

Thirty minutes with the founder. You'll leave with a clear picture of your market, what a campaign would look like and what it would cost.

Or email sales@beleaded.com

# Off-market deal flow for M&A advisors and business brokers

Be Leaded finds owners of privately held companies who may be open to a sale, a recapitalization or a valuation, and starts confidential conversations in your firm's name. You get meetings with owners who want to talk. We don't advise on transactions. Your team does.

## The best deals are rarely listed.

Many owners of solid businesses never put them on the market. When they do sell, it's often to the advisor or buyer who reached them first and treated the conversation with care. That's the conversation we start for you.

### The list

A database export filtered by industry and headcount. Half the owners already sold, retired or never owned the company.

Owners researched against your mandate: revenue band, tenure, ownership and signals that a conversation could be timely.

### The approach

"We have a buyer for your business." Owners hear it every week and delete it on sight.

A short, respectful note from a real person at your firm, with something true about the business and no pressure.

### The follow-through

Every reply lands on an advisor's desk, including the curious, the unqualified and the angry.

We screen replies for intent and book meetings only with owners who asked for one and fit your mandate.

## What we deliver

Everything between your mandate and a first meeting with an owner. You don't need to buy data, tools or inboxes.

### Owner lists built to your mandate

Industry, geography, revenue band, years in business and ownership, researched and verified before a single email goes out.

### Outreach in your firm's name

Email and LinkedIn from sending domains tied to your brand, written in your voice. You approve every message.

### Timing signals

We prioritize owners where timing may be right: long tenure, no named successor, a first general manager, a second site.

### Replies screened for intent

Serious owners are separated from curiosity before anything reaches your calendar. Every reply is visible to you.

### Meetings on your calendar

Valuation calls and introductions with owners who asked for them, booked directly with your advisors.

### Confidential by default

No listings, no public owner names, and no mention of a client or buyer unless you approve it.

How we approach owners

## Short, specific and respectful.

Owners of good businesses are approached constantly. The ones who reply are answering a person who clearly knows their business and isn't in a hurry.

- A short note from a real person at your firm
- Curiosity about the business, with no claim that a buyer is waiting
- An offer of a confidential valuation or a short conversation
- Easy to decline, and opt-outs honored right away

## Who we work with

Sell-side

### M&A advisors

Owner conversations that turn into engagements, sourced to the sectors and size range your firm covers.

Main Street and lower middle market

### Business brokers

A steady flow of owners open to a valuation, so listings come from conversations instead of referrals alone.

Buy-side

### Buyers and sponsors

Independent sponsors, search funds, family offices and platform companies looking for add-on acquisitions.

## How it works

From your mandate to owner conversations in about three weeks.

- Day 1 Mandate call Sectors, geography, size range, deal types and what a qualified owner conversation means to your firm.
- Days 2 to 14 Build Owner research, verification, sending domains, warmup and the first sequences for your approval.
- Week 3 Outreach Email and LinkedIn go live at a careful pace. Replies are screened and meetings booked.
- Every week Report Owners contacted, replies, meetings and the conversations in progress.

Clear lines

## We start conversations. Your team runs the deal.

Our job ends when an owner is on your calendar. Everything after that belongs to your advisors.

- We don't advise on transactions, value businesses or negotiate terms
- We don't list businesses or publish owner names
- We don't claim a buyer exists when one doesn't
- We don't contact an owner again after they opt out

## Questions about deal flow

Ask anything else on the call.

**What is off-market deal sourcing?**

Off-market deal sourcing means finding companies that aren't listed for sale and reaching their owners directly. Many privately held businesses are never formally marketed, so an advisor or buyer who starts the conversation early can talk to the owner before a formal process begins.

**How do you find owners who might sell?**

We research companies that match your mandate by industry, geography, revenue band, tenure and ownership, then prioritize owners showing signals such as no named successor, a first general manager hire or a founder who still runs sales. Every contact is verified before outreach.

**Do you reach out in our firm's name?**

Yes. We set up sending domains tied to your brand and write in your voice. You approve every email before it sends, and meetings are booked directly with your advisors.

**Is the outreach confidential?**

Yes. We never name a client or a buyer without your approval, we never publish owner names, and owner data stays private to your engagement.

**Which industries do you cover?**

Any industry with privately held companies in your size range. Common mandates include home and commercial services, manufacturing, distribution, healthcare services and business services.

**Do you work with buyers as well as advisors?**

Yes. Independent sponsors, search funds, family offices and platform companies use the same process to source add-on acquisitions directly from owners.

**What does it cost?**

Programs start at $2,000 a month. The exact number depends on the size of your mandate and the channels we run, and you'll have it after a 30-minute call.

Thirty minutes with the founder. You'll leave with a clear picture of your market, what a campaign would look like and what it would cost.

### Paid social and search
Ads with the follow-up built in.

### Newsletters, email and SMS
Newsletters people open.

### AI voice follow-up
Every lead called back within a minute.

## Questions

**How do you reactivate lapsed dental patients?**

A short text or email to patients 12 to 18 months past their last visit, with one reason to rebook and a booking link, sent only to patients who agreed to be contacted.

**Is this compliant with patient privacy rules?**

Marketing lists hold names and contact details only. We never use treatment or health information in targeting or copy, and your practice keeps control of the patient data. Have your counsel review the consent language.

**What works for med spa marketing?**

Meta ads with one seasonal treatment offer, a booking page, follow-up within minutes, and a newsletter that shows results and answers common questions.

**Do you work with multi-location groups?**

Yes. Each location gets its own edition and offers, and the group gets one weekly report.

# Lead generation for M&A advisors and business brokers

Owners of good businesses don't list them. They talk to the advisor who reached them first and treated the conversation with care. We research owners to your mandate, write short, respectful outreach in your firm's name, screen replies for intent, and book owner conversations with your advisors.

## Who we reach

### Founder-owned companies in your size range

Filtered by industry, geography, revenue band and years in business.

### Owners showing timing signals

Long tenure, no named successor, a first general manager, a second site.

### Buy-side clients

Independent sponsors, search funds and platform companies sourcing add-ons.

## What works in M&A and brokers

The specifics that make the difference between a campaign that books meetings and one that gets ignored.

- Owner research from filings, websites and press, verified before outreach
- A note about the business, an offer of a confidential valuation, never a fictional buyer
- Email and LinkedIn from domains and profiles tied to your firm
- Replies screened so only serious owners reach an advisor
- A quarterly owner newsletter for everyone who said not now

## Programs we run for m&a and brokers

Owner conversations for advisors and brokers.

Outreach from your team's own profiles.

### Newsletters, email and SMS
Newsletters people open.

## Questions

**How do you find business owners who might sell?**

We build lists to your mandate and prioritize owners with timing signals: long tenure, no named successor, a recent general manager hire, a second location. Then we approach each one personally.

**Is the outreach confidential?**

Yes. We never name a client or a buyer without your approval, never publish owner names, and keep owner data private to your engagement.

**How many owner conversations should we expect?**

A handful a month per mandate from a well-researched list, growing as the not-now pile matures. Owner outreach replies at lower rates than B2B email, but each reply is worth far more.

**Do you advise on the deal?**

No. We start the conversations. Your team runs the deal.

# Not sure who to hire? We'll match you.

Tell us what you need. Within one business day you get an introduction to a partner we've checked ourselves: an outbound agency in another region or language, an email or CRM platform, a paid ads specialist, a web studio, or a capital or M&A advisor. Free for you. Partners pay us only for qualified introductions, so we only introduce what fits.

## Build your request in thirty seconds

Pick what applies. The request writes itself below, and you can send it or book a call.

### I need help with

### Monthly budget

### Timeline

### Your request

Sends to sales@beleaded.com. If your email app doesn't open, copy the request and paste it into a new email.

## How it works

Three steps, one introduction, no fee to you.

- Day 1 Tell us what you need Send the request above or book a call. We ask a few questions about your buyer, budget and what a good outcome looks like.
- Day 1 to 2 We check fit We match against partners whose references and results we've checked, and rule out anyone who isn't right for your size, market or budget.
- Within a business day One introduction A warm email introduction to one partner, with why we chose them. If the first isn't right, we make a second. That's it.

Why it's free for you

## Partners pay for introductions. You don't.

Each partner pays a fee per qualified introduction, agreed with us up front. We tell you that on every introduction, and we never take a listing fee, so nobody buys their way onto the list.

- Every partner has given references we've spoken to and results we've checked
- One introduction at a time, never a spreadsheet of vendors
- The partner relationship is disclosed on every introduction
- If we can do the work ourselves, we'll say so and let you choose
- No fee to you, ever

For partners

## Join the network. Pay only for qualified introductions.

Agencies, platforms, consultants and advisors with real results and a clear specialty. We're taking applications now.

### What we ask of partners

- Two or more client references we can call
- Results you can show, in the specialty you claim
- A clear fit: region, language, industry, budget range or tool
- A per-introduction fee agreed up front. No listing fees.
- A reply to every introduction within one business day

## Questions about Match

**What is Be Leaded Match?**

A free matching service for companies that need an agency, a tool, a consultant or an advisor. You tell us what you need, we check fit against partners whose references and results we've verified, and we make one warm introduction. Partners pay a fee per qualified introduction, which we disclose.

**Is it really free?**

Yes, for the company asking. Partners pay us per qualified introduction, and there are no listing fees, so nobody pays to be recommended.

**What if Be Leaded could do the work?**

We'll say so and lay out both options. Some needs are ours to run, such as cold email and newsletters. Many aren't, such as outbound in a language we don't write, a CRM implementation or a capital raise, and those go to partners.

**How do you vet partners?**

References we speak to, results we check, and a clear specialty. We also watch how they respond to introductions, and partners who go quiet are removed.

**Can you help an owner raise capital or sell?**

Yes. We introduce owners to capital partners and M&A advisors we've checked, and the partner relationship is disclosed. We don't advise on the transaction ourselves.

**How do partners join?**

Email us with your specialty, two references and examples of results. If it's a fit, we agree a per-introduction fee and add you to the network.

Delivery rate across the programs we run.

Average open rate on the newsletters we run.

Figures as of September 2026.

## Engagements

M&A advisory and business brokerage

### Off-market owner outreach for sell-side advisors

#### The brief

Advisors and brokers wanted more owner conversations than referrals could supply, without a single email that would embarrass the firm in front of an owner.

#### What we built

Owner lists researched to each mandate's industry, geography and size range. Outreach in the firm's voice by email and LinkedIn, from domains tied to its brand. Replies screened for intent before anything reached an advisor's calendar.

#### Where it landed

Off-market sourcing for advisors and brokers is the largest category of work we've delivered, and the reason we run it as its own program.

Software for countertop fabricators

### LinkedIn outreach to US fabricators, plus audience newsletters

#### The brief

Put a new kind of measuring software in front of owners and operations leads at countertop fabrication shops across the US.

#### What we built

A 2,000-contact prospect list filtered from a much larger raw export, with distributors, tool suppliers and cabinet-only shops removed and only decision-makers kept. LinkedIn sequences across three audiences: stone fabricators, CAD drafters and designers, and virtual tour providers. A separate newsletter for each audience.

#### Where it landed

An ongoing monthly retainer, with outreach running across all three audiences.

Outbound infrastructure

### Scaling outbound from 50,000 to 400,000 emails a day

#### The brief

Grow daily sending volume eightfold without losing the inbox.

#### What we built

Multi-domain sending infrastructure across Google Workspace and Microsoft inboxes, with SPF, DKIM and DMARC on every domain, staged warmup, and bounce and suppression management at scale.

#### Where it landed

Deliverability rose from about 88% to 99% or better as volume grew. Open rates held around 49%, response rates ran at 2% to 3%, and replies were worked through to booked demos.

- Emails a day: 400K
- Deliverability: 99%+
- Response rate: 2-3%

B2B demand generation firm

### A prospecting newsletter sent three times a week

#### The brief

Keep a large B2B audience engaged with frequent sends, without wearing out the list.

#### What we built

Three campaigns a week to about 5,000 recipients each, with list hygiene and unsubscribe handling on every send.

#### Where it landed

About 34,000 sends in 30 days. Open rates between 39% and 51%, unsubscribes between 0.10% and 0.50%, and no spam complaints.

- Sends in 30 days: ~34K
- Open rate: 39-51%
- Spam complaints: 0%

## What gets a newsletter opened

The same few things show up in every program that works.

### A sender people recognize

A real name and a brand the reader knows, sent from a domain that's authenticated and consistent.

### A subject line that says what's inside

Specific beats clever. Readers open when they know what they're getting.

### One idea per issue

A single useful point, made well, with one clear next step at the end.

### A clean list

Bounces and complaints suppressed, and quiet subscribers re-engaged or removed before they drag placement down.

### A schedule readers expect

Same day, same time, so the newsletter becomes a habit rather than a surprise.

### Design that survives every inbox

Built for Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail, on phones and in dark mode, with text that still reads when images are off.

# Pricing

Programs start at $2,000 a month. For the right fit, we price per qualified meeting instead. You'll have an exact number after a 30-minute call.

Monthly program

From $2,000 a month

A defined program for a fixed monthly fee. Best when you want outbound running every week without hiring.

- Sending domains, inboxes and warmup
- List building and verification
- Sequences written for your market
- LinkedIn alongside email
- Reply handling and booking
- Weekly reporting

Pay per meeting

For the right fit

You pay for meetings that match a definition we agree in writing before launch. Best for a clear buyer and an offer that already sells.

- Qualified meeting defined up front
- The same infrastructure, data and team
- Priced after we review your market

## What changes the price

Four things, and we'll walk through each of them on the call.

### Market size and volume

How many accounts fit your buyer, and how many inboxes it takes to reach them at a safe pace.

### Channels

Email alone, or email with LinkedIn, paid social and search, newsletters, SMS or voice. Ad spend and call minutes are paid at cost, on top of the fee.

### Offers and segments

One offer to one buyer, or several offers to different segments, each with its own list and copy.

### Replies and booking

Whether we handle every reply and book meetings, or hand warm replies to your team.

## Compared with hiring an SDR

What the same budget looks like either way.

|  | In-house SDR | Be Leaded |
| Cost | Median on-target earnings of $80,000 a year, before benefits, tools, data and management time | From $2,000 a month, with tools, data and infrastructure included |
| Time to first meetings | Average ramp of 3.0 months | Live in about three weeks |
| Continuity | Average tenure of 1.9 years, with 40% median annual attrition | A team that stays on your program |
| Infrastructure | You buy and maintain domains, inboxes, data and tools | Built, warmed and monitored for you |

SDR figures from The Bridge Group's 2025 SDR report. An in-house rep does things we don't, such as live discovery calls inside your team. This comparison is about cost and time to first meetings.

## Questions about pricing

**Why don't you publish one fixed price?**

Because the work depends on your market. Reaching 800 accounts in one niche is a different program from reaching 30,000 across several segments. We'd rather give you an exact number after a 30-minute call than a price that doesn't fit.

**Do you guarantee meetings?**

We don't promise a number before we've looked at your market and your offer. For the right fit, we price per qualified meeting, so you only pay for meetings that match the definition we agree on.

**Do we need to buy tools, data or inboxes?**

No. Sending domains, inboxes, warmup, data, verification and the tools we run on are included in the program.

**How soon will we see meetings?**

Most programs go live in about three weeks, once domains are warmed and the first sequences are approved. How quickly replies turn into meetings depends on your market and your offer.

**Can we start with one channel?**

Yes. Starting with email and adding LinkedIn, paid social, newsletters, SMS or voice later is common, and the price reflects what you run.

**How is ad spend handled?**

Ad spend is paid to Meta, Google or LinkedIn directly and isn't part of our fee. The same goes for call minutes on voice programs, which are billed at cost.

**Do you work with companies outside the US?**

Yes. We run programs in the US and internationally, and we check local rules before sending into the EU, the UK or Canada.

Free tool

# Outbound calculator

Move the sliders. The calculator sizes the sending infrastructure a cold email program needs and estimates the meetings it should produce, using the same rules we use to plan client programs: 25 to 50 emails per inbox a day, two or three inboxes per domain, and the reply-rate bands from the 2026 benchmark reports.

## Your program

## Your infrastructure

## Your results

Each box is a sending domain. Each bar inside it is an inbox.

Estimates. Replies and bounces remove people from the sequence, so real send counts run 15% to 25% under these figures. Every market is different, and we'll give you a range for yours on a call.

## How the math works

The rules behind the numbers, with sources.

**Why 25 to 50 emails per inbox?**

Hunter's 2025 data found inboxes sending 20 to 49 emails a day replied 27% above average, while volumes over 100 a day hurt deliverability. Our programs run 25 to 50 per inbox with warmup on top. Read how many cold emails to send per day.

**Why two or three inboxes per domain?**

Domain reputation is shared by every inbox on it. Keeping each domain at 100 to 150 cold emails a day limits the damage if one has a bad week, and stays far below Gmail's 5,000-a-day bulk sender line.

**Where do the reply and meeting rates come from?**

Instantly's 2026 benchmark report puts the average reply rate at 3.43% of emails sent, with the top quartile above 5.5%. Across our programs about a third of replies are positive and about half of those become held meetings. See the cold email benchmarks guide.

**What isn't in the cost?**

Data, verification, the sending platform, warmup, copy and the people running it. The infrastructure line is only domains and inboxes, so you can see how cheap the plumbing is compared with the work.

- FAQ

# Frequently asked questions

The questions we hear on first calls, answered plainly. If yours isn't here, ask us.

## Working with Be Leaded

**What does Be Leaded do?**

Be Leaded is a B2B marketing agency based in New York. We run cold email and appointment setting, LinkedIn outreach, paid social and search, newsletter, email and SMS programs, AI voice follow-up, and off-market deal flow for M&A advisors and business brokers. We build the infrastructure, write every message and book meetings on your calendar.

**How does a program start?**

With a 30-minute call. We learn your buyer, your offer and what a qualified meeting means to you, and you leave with a realistic view of what a campaign can do. If it's a fit, we send a one-page scope and start the build the same week.

**How long until we see meetings?**

Most outbound programs go live in about three weeks, once domains are warmed and the first sequences are approved. Paid programs produce leads within days of launch. Newsletters take longer to pay off and keep paying.

**Who will we work with?**

Ahmad Khan, the founder, takes every first call and stays on every account. A small team handles list research, verification and campaign operations.

**Do we approve the emails?**

Yes. Every list and every message is approved by you before it sends, and you can read every reply.

**Can we speak to a current client?**

Yes, after a first call. Client names stay private on the website, but we connect prospective clients with current ones.

## Cold email and LinkedIn

**What counts as a qualified meeting?**

We agree on it in writing before launch: title, company size, industry and the problem the person needs solved. We only book meetings that match.

**Will cold email hurt our company domain?**

No. We send from separate domains that we set up, warm and monitor every day. Your company domain never carries cold volume.

**How many emails do you send?**

It depends on your market. Each inbox sends 25 to 50 cold emails a day and we add inboxes and domains as a program grows. Our infrastructure can carry more than 400,000 emails a day.

**Is cold email legal?**

In the US, yes, under CAN-SPAM: accurate headers, an honest subject line, a physical postal address, a way to opt out and opt-outs honored within 10 business days. The law applies to B2B email too. Rules differ in the EU, UK and Canada, and we check them before sending there.

**Is LinkedIn outreach safe for our accounts?**

We send from your team's own profiles at a human pace, inside LinkedIn's limits of roughly 100 invitations a week, and never run mass automation on an account.

**Do you guarantee a number of meetings?**

We don't promise a number before we've looked at your market. For the right fit, we price per qualified meeting so you only pay for meetings that match the definition we agreed on.

## Paid ads, newsletters, SMS and voice

**How much ad spend do we need?**

Usually at least $1,500 a month per platform so Meta or Google has enough data to learn. Ad spend is paid to the platforms directly and isn't part of our fee.

**Do you build the landing pages?**

Yes. Fast pages built for one offer, with a form that captures consent so we can follow up by text and voice.

**What open rate do your newsletters get?**

The programs we run average 49%, against a 2025 industry median of 43.46% in MailerLite's benchmark. We judge newsletters on clicks, replies and unsubscribes as well, because privacy features inflate opens.

**Can you text our customers?**

Only people who gave consent on your form. We register your number for business texting, honor STOP automatically and never text purchased lists.

**Can the AI voice agent make cold calls?**

No. Calls with an AI-generated voice need prior express consent under the TCPA, so the agent only calls leads and customers who asked to be contacted.

## Pricing and terms

**What does it cost?**

Programs start at $2,000 a month. Paid programs add ad spend, and voice programs add call minutes at cost. You'll have an exact number after a 30-minute call. See pricing.

**Is there a minimum term?**

Outbound programs take about three weeks to build and a few more to read, so we ask for enough time to judge them fairly. We'll set the term out plainly in the scope before you sign anything.

**What do we keep if we stop?**

Your lists, your copy and your reports. Sending domains and inboxes are set up in your name where possible, and we set out ownership in writing before the program starts.

**Do you work with companies outside the US?**

Yes. We run programs in the US and internationally, and we check local rules before sending into the EU, UK or Canada.

# Outbound and email marketing glossary

35 terms from cold email, deliverability, LinkedIn, SMS and lead generation, defined the way we'd explain them on a call. Each links to the guide that goes deeper.

- A2P 10DLC: Application-to-person messaging over standard 10-digit long code numbers in the US. Carriers require businesses to register their brand and campaign through The Campaign Registry before texting from these numbers, and filter unregistered traffic. Read more
- Appointment setting: The work of turning a reply into a held meeting: qualifying the prospect, handling the back and forth and putting a time on the calendar. At Be Leaded it's part of every outbound program. Read more
- Bounce rate: The share of emails that couldn't be delivered. Hard bounces are invalid addresses, soft bounces are temporary. Keep it under 2% by verifying every address before sending. Read more
- Bulk sender: Gmail's term for anyone sending more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail accounts. Bulk senders must authenticate with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, keep spam rates under 0.3% and support one-click unsubscribe. The status never expires. Read more
- CAN-SPAM: The US law governing commercial email. It requires accurate headers, an honest subject line, a physical postal address, a working opt-out and opt-outs honored within 10 business days. It applies to B2B email, and each violating email can draw a penalty of up to $53,088. Read more
- Catch-all domain: A domain that accepts email to any address, valid or not, so verification tools can't confirm individual addresses. Catch-all contacts are held for later, smaller sends or checked with a second tool. Read more
- Cold email: An unsolicited business email to someone who hasn't heard from you before, sent one to one with a specific reason. Distinct from a newsletter, which goes to people who subscribed. Read more
- Cost per meeting: Total program cost divided by qualified meetings held. The number that matters more than cost per lead or cost per click. Read more
- Deliverability: Whether email reaches the inbox rather than spam or the void. Decided by authentication, sender reputation, list quality, content and volume. Read more
- Delivery rate: The share of emails accepted by the receiving server. Not the same as inbox placement, which is where the email lands once accepted. Be Leaded's programs hold a 99% delivery rate. Read more
- DKIM: DomainKeys Identified Mail. A cryptographic signature added to each email and checked against a key published in the sender's DNS, proving the message wasn't altered in transit. Read more
- DMARC: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance. A DNS policy that tells receivers what to do when SPF and DKIM fail and where to send reports. Required by Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft for bulk senders, with p=none the minimum. Read more
- Domain reputation: A mailbox provider's running score of a sending domain, built from complaint rates, bounces, engagement and authentication history. Visible in Google Postmaster Tools. Read more
- Email verification: Checking whether an address exists and accepts mail before sending to it, using tools such as ZeroBounce or MillionVerifier. The first defense against bounces. Read more
- Inbox placement: Where an accepted email lands: primary inbox, promotions, spam. Measured with seed lists and placement tests, and improved by warmup, authentication and clean lists. Read more
- Lead: A person or company that has shown interest or fits your buyer profile. An inbound lead asked for something. An outbound lead is one you chose to contact. Read more
- Lifecycle email: Automated emails triggered by what a person does: a welcome series, an onboarding sequence, a re-engagement flow. Runs between newsletter issues. Read more
- List-unsubscribe: An email header that lets mailbox providers show an unsubscribe button. Gmail and Yahoo require the one-click version (RFC 8058) for bulk senders, with requests honored within two days. Read more
- Newsletter: A recurring email to people who subscribed, with one useful idea per issue. The programs Be Leaded runs average a 49% open rate. Read more
- Off-market deal: A company that isn't listed for sale, reached by approaching the owner directly. Most privately held businesses change hands this way. Read more
- Open rate: The share of delivered emails recorded as opened. Inflated by privacy features such as Apple Mail Privacy Protection, so it's a trend line rather than a truth. Judge campaigns on replies and meetings. Read more
- Outbound: Marketing and sales activity where you reach out first: cold email, LinkedIn outreach, calls. The opposite of inbound, where the prospect finds you. Read more
- Positive reply rate: The share of emails that get a reply expressing interest, as opposed to any reply at all. About a third of replies are positive in a typical program. Read more
- Prior express written consent: The consent standard under the TCPA for marketing texts and automated or AI-voice calls: a clear written agreement, not pre-checked, that the person will receive marketing messages from your business. Read more
- Qualified meeting: A meeting with someone who matches a definition agreed in writing before launch: title, company size, industry and the problem they need solved. Read more
- Reply rate: Replies divided by emails sent. Instantly's 2026 report puts the average at 3.43%, the top quartile above 5.5%. Different tools count differently, so check the method before comparing. Read more
- SDR: Sales development representative. The person who prospects and books meetings for account executives. Median on-target earnings of $80,000 a year and a 3.0-month ramp, according to The Bridge Group. Read more
- Sending domain: A domain used only for outbound email, separate from a company's main domain, so cold volume never touches the domain that carries invoices and support. Read more
- Sequence: A series of touches to one prospect over days or weeks: emails, LinkedIn messages, sometimes a call. Four to seven touches is the range the data supports. Read more
- Spam complaint rate: The share of delivered emails that recipients mark as spam. Gmail asks senders to stay under 0.1% and never reach 0.3%. Yahoo's line is 0.3%. Read more
- Speed to lead: The time between a lead arriving and your first contact. Reaching a lead within five minutes rather than thirty raises the odds of contact roughly a hundredfold, per the original lead response study. Read more
- SPF: Sender Policy Framework. A DNS record listing the servers allowed to send email for a domain. Keep it under 10 DNS lookups and aligned with the From domain. Read more
- TCPA: The Telephone Consumer Protection Act, the US law covering marketing calls and texts. It requires prior express written consent for marketing texts and for calls made with automated or artificial voices, including AI voices. Read more
- Warmup: Sending a small, rising volume of email from a new inbox for two to three weeks so mailbox providers learn it's legitimate before it carries cold volume. Kept running at a low level afterward. Read more
- White label: Work delivered under another company's brand. Be Leaded runs outbound and newsletter programs for marketing agencies under the agency's name. Read more

## Tell us who you want to meet.

Thirty minutes with the founder. You'll leave with a clear picture of your market, what a campaign would look like and what it would cost.

Cold email

# How to book more SaaS demos with cold email

By Ahmad Khan, founder of Be Leaded. Updated October 5, 2026. 9 min read.

The short answer: Book more SaaS demos by writing to one buyer about one real trigger, from a verified list on a warmed domain, then putting an interested reply on a calendar the same business day. A demo counts when your account executive and the buyer can both see the hold, and the buyer matches a definition you wrote before the first send. Track reply rate, positive reply rate, demos booked, and show rate. Do not track opens.

- ICP and the buying trigger
- List building and verification
- Inbox and domain setup
- The demo email
- Follow-up cadence
- Turn replies into demos
- What to measure
- Common mistakes
- Agency or in house
- Checklist
- FAQ
- Sources

## Pick the ICP and one buying trigger

Cold email for SaaS fails when the list is "companies that might use software." A useful ICP is narrow enough that the first line could only be true of that account. SaaS demo booking starts here, not in the subject line. Write these four lines before you buy a contact.

| Line | Write this | Not ready if |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Company | Industry, headcount band, and the tools they already run | The list is "anyone in B2B" |
| Person | The title that owns the problem, plus at most one person who can bring them in | You plan to email five titles at one company this week |
| Qualified demo | Title, company size, industry, and a stated problem | Any reply would count as a demo |
| Buying trigger | One change that makes this month different from last month | The only reason to write is that the company exists |

On B2B SaaS programs the company filter is headcount, tech stack, funding, locations, and tools already in place. Ops software for 50 to 200 person teams is a different list from finance software for CFOs. Your account executive takes the demo. One or two names per company.

Write the qualified demo before launch: title, company size, industry, and a stated problem. The trigger is one change this month (a new tool, funding, headcount, a location, a new buyer). If you cannot name it in a sentence, do not write. Product-led teams use the same shape: the first line is about usage, and outbound reaches accounts that will not show up through self-serve.

## Build the list, then verify every address

List building is filtering. Pull accounts that match the four lines, then the person who owns the problem. Apollo and Clay are tools we use for that research. The filter matters more than the vendor.

- Verify every address before the first send. Catch-all and unverifiable addresses stay off the list. A bounce is a reputation problem. ZeroBounce or MillionVerifier is the usual check.
- One record per person. If two sources disagree on the title, check the company site or LinkedIn before you mail them.
- Remove customers, open opportunities, active trials, partners, and anyone who already said no. A cold demo ask to a current customer burns trust inside your own company.
- Two columns or the row does not send: the trigger, and the one detail the email will use.

A few hundred clean rows beat ten thousand dirty ones. Fit is the constraint, not volume. Be Leaded's sending infrastructure can handle more than 400,000 emails a day at a 99% delivery rate, across 30-plus client programs, from New York. That capacity is for more of the right accounts. It is not permission to widen the ICP.

## Set up the inbox, then use the guides you already have

Cold mail does not leave the domain that sends invoices, password resets, and product email. Use separate sending domains, with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, and warm them first. The records and the complaint-rate lines are in the cold email deliverability guide. The ramp, two to three weeks then a low level that stays on, is in the email warmup guide.

- Approve every sequence before it sends. Plain text, one ask, no images.
- Keep new inboxes at a low daily volume. Add inboxes when you need reach. Do not push a young one.
- Plan on about three weeks to launch: domains, authentication, warmup, a verified list, and approved copy.

## Write a short email whose only job is a demo

The first email earns a reply. The note you send after they answer puts the demo on a calendar. Mixing those two jobs is how a first touch turns into a landing page.

- Subject: the trigger or their company, in a few words. Not "quick question," not "demo," and not your product name.
- First line: one detail only they would recognize. A tool, a hiring post, a change you can point at.
- Second line: the problem that detail implies, in their words, not your category.
- One sentence on the demo: 20 or 30 minutes, who attends (their buyer and your account executive), and what you will look at. Not a product tour.
- One ask: a question they can answer in a line. No deck, no second link, no "learn more."

Keep the first email under about 80 words. Instantly's 2026 benchmark report found that the best-performing first emails run under 80 words, and that 58% of replies come from the first step. Later steps cannot rescue a brochure. More patterns are in the cold email templates. Copy the structure, not someone else's sentences.

Names and companies in the two examples below are made up. They show the shape of a demo email. They are not client results.

Subject: the new WMS

Jordan, Northline posted for a WMS admin last month, so the cutover is probably still messy.

We spend demo time on the orders a new system drops, with the head of ops and our account executive, for 20 minutes. Not a tour.

Is that a problem on your floor this month?

Alex

If you had to invent the hiring post, delete the row.

Subject: 12 new AEs

Priya, you added about a dozen account executives this quarter. Ramp usually breaks before the CRM does.

Twenty minutes with your RevOps lead and our account executive, on the stages where new reps lose deals.

Worth a look, or should I write to someone else?

Alex

If they name someone else, thank them, stop, and write that person a new first email. Do not forward the old pitch. Two times and one calendar link wait until they reply.

## Follow up on a cadence, then stop

Seven touches over about four weeks: day 1, 4, 7, 11, 15, 21, and 28. Two sit on LinkedIn. Early gaps are three or four days. Later gaps are about a week. The last email says you will stop. What each touch says is in the cold email follow-up sequence. Hunter's study, cited there, found three-email sequences reply at 6.8% against 3.3% for one email. For a demo, touch 2 adds one new fact in the same thread, touch 4 asks who owns the demo if the title was wrong, and touch 6 carries one proof you can stand behind (separate domains at a 99% delivery rate), not "companies like yours."

LinkedIn lead generation fills the gaps: a short note, no calendar link, no pitch on the request, from a real profile, near roughly 100 invitations a week. The user agreement prohibits bots. Do not send both channels the same day. A reply on either one stops the other, and the sequence ends that day.

## Turn an interested reply into a booked demo the same day

An interested reply with nothing on a calendar is not a booked demo. Appointment setting is the work after the reply: check it against the definition, handle the back and forth, and put a hold where your sellers will see it.

On our programs the rule is the same business day.

- Stop the sequence before you reply. If the tool will not, a person does.
- Answer what they asked. Do not paste the first email again.
- Two times in their time zone, and one booking link. Name the account executive. "Tuesday, 10:30 a.m. your time (Eastern)."
- Send the invite from the seller's calendar. Company, why they replied, and whether they match. No deck.
- No time chosen: one reminder the next business morning, then wait.
- Log it. Salesforce, HubSpot, or your CRM is the record. The sequencer is not.

A maybe gets one question, then times if they still want the call. A not-now gets a return date and a stop. The next note on that date is a new first email. A wrong person gets one referral ask. Unsubscribe and a hard no come off email and LinkedIn the same day. The full sort is in how to turn cold email replies into meetings.

Show rate is decided here. A long form before the times, a 7 a.m. slot on their side, or a second reschedule books a demo nobody attends. After a no-show: two new times the same day, one note the next morning, then stop.

## What to measure

Judge the program on four numbers. Leave opens off the report.

| Number | What it is | What to do with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reply rate | Replies divided by emails sent | About 3% is healthy here. Below that, change the list or the angle before you add volume. |
| Positive reply rate | Replies that want a conversation | About a third of replies are positive. If replies rise and interest does not, fix the list or the ask. |
| Demos booked | A hold both sides can see, matching the definition | A positive reply is not a demo. Plan on five to eight meetings per 1,000 well-targeted emails. |
| Show rate | Held demos divided by demos booked | If they book and do not show, fix the calendar and who is on the call before you rewrite email one. |

Published reply rates are not one number. Instantly's 2026 report puts the average at 3.43%. A 0.45% figure from another study is a different counting method. The benchmarks guide walks through both. Compare your program to itself, week to week, with one definition.

That five-to-eight range is the planning model on our B2B SaaS page and in the benchmarks guide: a typical reply rate, about a third of replies positive, and about half of those becoming meetings. It is a model, not a promise. We also hold infrastructure to a 99% delivery rate. If delivery falls, fix authentication, the list, or volume per inbox before you rewrite the copy.

## Mistakes that keep demos off the calendar

- Mailing a feature list to a title you never defined.
- Buying a list and sending the same day, with no verification and no warmup.
- Sending from the company domain because the test is "small." A small test still teaches mailbox providers who you are.
- Putting the word demo, a tracking pixel, and a deck in email one.
- Following up with "just checking in" and the same paragraph.
- Leaving the next sequence step on after they reply.
- Counting a positive reply, or a link you sent, as a booked demo.
- Emailing the whole leadership team because the first person was quiet.
- Adding volume because the quarter is behind. Fix the ICP or the trigger first. Fifty meetings from 1,000 emails does not match the planning range above.

## When to hire an agency, and when to build it in house

Build it in house when someone will own the list, the copy, the inboxes, and same-day replies, and a few hundred careful emails a month are the plan. If nobody owns the reply, the program stalls on the first yes.

Hire when any of these are true:

- Nobody on the team will answer a positive reply the same business day.
- You need separate domains, warmup, and a verified list, and you do not want that project on the domain that runs the product.
- Account executives should be on demos, not building spreadsheets.
- You want a written definition of a qualified demo, every reply visible, and a weekly report on the four numbers above.

Hire a firm that shows you the list and the copy before anything sends, and that counts a meeting only when it matches the definition. The best cold email agency scorecard is the comparison: deliverability, separate domains, qualified meetings, pricing, and fit.

Cold email and appointment setting programs start at $2,000 a month. Pay-per-meeting pricing is available for the right fit. You get an exact number after a 30-minute call. What the monthly fee covers is on the pricing page. If you want to talk through the market before that call, use the contact page.

Be Leaded does this from New York: lists by tech stack and headcount, sequences you approve, and qualified demos on your account executives' calendars. Ahmad Khan takes the first call.

## Checklist before you scale

- ICP in one sentence: industry, headcount, tools.
- One buyer title. A second name only if they can bring that person to the demo.
- Qualified demo written down: title, company size, industry, stated problem.
- Every row has a trigger and one true detail.
- Customers, open deals, trials, partners, and opt-outs are removed.
- Every address is verified. Catch-alls are off the list.
- Separate domains, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and warmup finished. If not, stop.
- First email under about 80 words, one ask, no deck.
- Seven touches. The sequence stops when a person replies.
- Interested replies get two times and one link the same business day.
- Weekly report: reply rate, positive reply rate, demos booked, show rate.
- Someone is named as the owner of the reply.

## FAQ

**How do you book more SaaS demos with cold email?**

Write to one ICP about one buying trigger, send from a verified list on a warmed domain, keep the first email short, follow the cadence, and put an interested reply on a calendar the same business day.

**What should a cold email for a SaaS demo include?**

One true detail, the problem it implies, who attends, and one question. Under about 80 words. The calendar link waits for the reply. No deck and no feature list.

**How many cold emails does it take to book a SaaS demo?**

Plan on five to eight held meetings per 1,000 well-targeted emails. That model assumes a typical reply rate, about a third of replies positive, and about half of those becoming meetings. It is not a guarantee.

**What should a SaaS team measure on a cold email program?**

Reply rate, positive reply rate, demos booked, and show rate, every week. Healthy here is about a 3% reply rate with about a third of replies positive, and a 99% delivery rate. Do not use opens.

**Should a SaaS company hire a cold email agency or build the program in house?**

Build it in house if someone will own the list, the inboxes, and same-day booking. Hire when account executives should be on demos. Programs start at $2,000 a month.

**What counts as a qualified SaaS demo?**

A meeting that matches a definition written before launch: title, company size, industry, and a stated problem. Your account executive takes the call. A reply alone is not a demo.
