Paid social

# Speed to lead: why the first five minutes decide your ad ROI, and how to automate it

By Ahmad Khan, founder of Be Leaded. Updated September 24, 2026. 4 min read.

The short answer: Speed to lead is the time between a lead arriving and your first contact, and it's the single biggest lever on paid advertising returns. The classic MIT/InsideSales study found the odds of reaching a lead dropped 100 times between 5 minutes and 30 minutes, and the Harvard Business Review audit of 2,241 companies found the average response took 42 hours while 23% never responded. Fix it with a text within a minute, a call within five, and an email sequence for anyone who goes quiet, all automated.

- What the studies found
- Why it matters most for paid leads
- The follow-up chain we build
- The consent that makes it legal
- What to measure
- A 30-minute audit of your own follow-up
- FAQ
- Sources

## What the studies found

| Study | Sample | Finding |
| MIT / InsideSales, Lead Response Management (2007) | 15,000+ leads, 100,000+ call attempts | Odds of contacting a lead fell 100 times between a call at 5 minutes and one at 30. Odds of qualifying fell 21 times. |
| Harvard Business Review, The Short Life of Online Sales Leads (2011) | 2,241 US companies audited with test leads | Firms that responded within an hour were nearly 7 times as likely to qualify the lead as those that waited even an hour longer. Average response time was 42 hours. 23% never responded. |
| Drift, Lead Response Survey (2017) | 433 B2B companies | 7% responded within 5 minutes. 55% hadn't responded after 5 business days. |

The numbers are old and nothing has changed. If anything, the lead now has more tabs open and more competitors one search away.

## Why it matters most for paid leads

A lead from a Meta instant form or a Google search ad is at peak intent for a few minutes. They asked a question, and they're waiting for an answer. The same person 42 hours later has had three other quotes and forgotten your ad. So every hour of delay silently raises your cost per customer while the cost per lead in your dashboard looks fine.

## The follow-up chain we build

| Time after lead | Channel | Message |
| Under 1 minute | Text | "Hi Mark, it's Rob at Copperline. Got your request. Tuesday or Wednesday?" Reply STOP to opt out. |
| 1 to 5 minutes | Call | An AI voice agent or a person. Confirms details, offers times, books. |
| 15 minutes | Email | Confirmation if booked. If not, the offer restated with a booking link. |
| Day 1, day 3, day 7 | Text and email | Short follow-ups with one question each, then stop. |
| Monthly | Newsletter | For everyone who said not now, so you're there when they're ready. |

Text first because it's read within minutes and doesn't interrupt. Call second because a conversation books the job. Email third because it carries the details. The whole chain is automated with n8n, and the call can be an AI voice agent when nobody is free.

## The consent that makes it legal

None of this is allowed unless the lead agreed to it. In the US, marketing texts and calls made with automated or artificial voices need prior express written consent under the TCPA, and the FCC confirmed in 2024 that AI-generated voices count as artificial. So the form has to say, in plain view, that submitting it means agreeing to texts and calls, with a way to opt out. We build that into every form and landing page, and STOP is honored automatically. See the SMS compliance guide.

## What to measure

- Median time to first contact, in minutes. If it's not under five, nothing else matters yet.
- Contact rate: the share of leads you actually reached.
- Booking rate: the share of leads with an appointment on the calendar.
- Cost per booked appointment, not cost per lead. The first number decides whether the ads are worth it.

## A 30-minute audit of your own follow-up

- Submit your own lead form from a phone at 2 PM on a weekday.
- Note when the first text, call and email arrive.
- Do it again at 7 PM and on Saturday morning.
- If any of the three took more than five minutes, you've found the leak in your ad budget.

Our paid social and search program builds the ads and the follow-up chain together, because the second half is where the money is.

## FAQ

**What is a good lead response time?**

Under five minutes. The original lead response study found the odds of reaching a lead fell 100 times between a call at five minutes and one at thirty, and companies responding within an hour were nearly seven times as likely to qualify the lead in the HBR audit.

**What is the average lead response time?**

The HBR audit of 2,241 companies found an average of 42 hours among companies that responded at all, and 23% never responded. Drift's later survey found only 7% of companies responded within five minutes.

**How do I respond to leads faster without hiring?**

Automate the first three touches: a text within a minute, a call from an AI voice agent within five, and an email at fifteen. Route anything the agent can't handle to a person.

**Can I text a lead who filled in a Facebook form?**

Only if the form captured consent to receive texts. Add clear consent language to the form or landing page, honor STOP automatically, and keep a record of the consent.

# SMS marketing compliance in 2026: TCPA, 10DLC and consent, explained plainly

By Ahmad Khan, founder of Be Leaded. Updated September 24, 2026. 4 min read.

The short answer: To send marketing texts in the US you need the recipient's prior express written consent under the TCPA, a business phone number registered for A2P 10DLC through your provider, automatic handling of STOP and HELP, sends during reasonable hours, and a record of every consent. The FCC's stricter one-to-one consent rule was vacated by the Eleventh Circuit in January 2025 and repealed by the FCC in July 2025, so the earlier consent standard applies. Never text purchased lists.

- Consent: the part that matters most
- What happened to the one-to-one consent rule
- A2P 10DLC registration
- STOP, HELP and quiet hours
- Content the carriers filter
- What a compliant program looks like
- Checklist before the first send
- FAQ
- Sources

We're not lawyers, and this isn't legal advice. It's the checklist we follow when we set up SMS programs for clients. Have counsel review your consent language before you send.

## Consent: the part that matters most

The Telephone Consumer Protection Act requires prior express written consent before sending marketing texts with an automated system. In practice that means the person typed their number into your form and agreed, in words they could read, to receive marketing texts from your business, with a note that consent isn't a condition of purchase and that message and data rates may apply. A checkbox that's pre-ticked doesn't count. A number scraped from a website doesn't count. A customer who bought something once doesn't count unless they agreed to texts.

Keep the record: what the form said, when the person submitted it, and from where. If a complaint arrives a year later, that record is your defense.

## What happened to the one-to-one consent rule

In late 2023 the FCC adopted a rule requiring consent to name each specific seller, which would have ended shared lead forms. The Eleventh Circuit vacated it in January 2025 in Insurance Marketing Coalition v. FCC, and the FCC formally repealed it in July 2025. The prior standard applies: prior express written consent, clearly disclosed, to the business doing the texting. Consent captured on your own form, for your own business, was always the safe route and still is.

## A2P 10DLC registration

US carriers require businesses that text from standard 10-digit numbers to register their brand and their campaign through The Campaign Registry, usually via the texting provider. Unregistered traffic is filtered or blocked. Registration takes a few days, asks what you'll send and how people opt in, and sets your daily throughput. Do it before the first send, and describe the campaign honestly, because the sample messages you submit are what the carriers expect to see.

## STOP, HELP and quiet hours

- STOP (and common variants) must end messages immediately and get a single confirmation reply. Under the FCC's revocation rules, any reasonable request to stop counts, not just the keyword.
- HELP must return your business name and a way to reach you.
- Identify yourself in the first message and in any message after a gap.
- Send during reasonable hours. Federal rules restrict telemarketing calls to 8 AM to 9 PM in the recipient's time zone, and several states are stricter for texts. We keep sends between 9 AM and 7 PM local unless the customer started the conversation.
- Frequency stated at opt-in and respected afterward.

## Content the carriers filter

Carrier rules block or throttle messages about cannabis, gambling, high-risk financial products and similar categories regardless of consent, and they penalize public URL shorteners, all-caps and messages that look like spam. Use your own branded short domain for links, write like a person, and keep it to one conversation per customer.

## What a compliant program looks like

Consent language on the form

By submitting, you agree to receive texts and calls, including automated and AI-assisted calls, from Northline Truck Buyers about your offer. Consent isn't a condition of purchase. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out, HELP for help.

First text

Hi Mark, it's Sam at Northline Truck Buyers. You asked for an offer on your 2019 F-250. Still thinking about selling? Reply STOP to opt out.

One thread per customer, a person's name, a reason the text exists, and the opt-out in the first message. This is the shape of the SMS programs we run.

## Checklist before the first send

- Consent language on every form, reviewed by counsel
- Consent records stored with timestamp and source
- Brand and campaign registered for A2P 10DLC
- STOP, HELP and reasonable opt-out requests handled automatically
- Business name in the first message
- Sends limited to reasonable local hours
- Branded link domain, no public shorteners
- No purchased or scraped numbers, ever

## FAQ

**Is SMS marketing legal in the US?**

Yes, with prior express written consent from each recipient, a number registered for A2P 10DLC, and automatic handling of opt-outs. Texting people who didn't agree exposes you to TCPA claims, which are brought per message.

**Do I need 10DLC registration to text customers?**

Yes, if you send business texts from a standard 10-digit US number. Carriers filter or block unregistered application-to-person traffic. Your texting provider handles the registration through The Campaign Registry.

**Can I text someone who filled in a lead form?**

Only if the form clearly disclosed that they'd receive texts and they agreed. Add the consent language to the form itself, not just to a linked privacy policy.

**What is the one-to-one consent rule?**

An FCC rule that would have required consent to name each specific seller. The Eleventh Circuit vacated it in January 2025 and the FCC repealed it in July 2025. The earlier prior express written consent standard applies.

## Sources

- FCC, Telemarketing and robocalls (TCPA)
- Womble Bond Dickinson, FCC repeals one-to-one consent rule following Eleventh Circuit decision
- The Campaign Registry, A2P 10DLC
- CTIA, Messaging Principles and Best Practices
- FCC, AI-generated voices in robocalls are artificial under the TCPA

# Cold email deliverability in 2026: what Gmail, Yahoo and Outlook require

By Ahmad Khan, founder of Be Leaded. Updated September 24, 2026.

The short answer: authenticate every sending domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, keep your spam complaint rate under 0.1% and never let it reach 0.3%, give every recipient an easy way to opt out, send from separate domains warmed for two to three weeks, verify every address before it goes out, and keep daily volume per inbox low. Gmail and Yahoo have required this of bulk senders since February 2024. Microsoft began rejecting non-compliant mail to Outlook.com addresses on May 5, 2025, and Gmail began rejecting non-compliant traffic in November 2025.

- The rules at a glance
- Does this apply to cold email?
- Send from separate domains
- Set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC
- Warm up every new inbox
- Keep volume per inbox low
- Verify every address
- Write like a person
- Monitor every day
- Checklist
- FAQ
- Sources

## The rules at a glance

Three mailbox providers set the rules most senders live by. Here is what each one requires today.

| Requirement | Gmail | Yahoo | Outlook.com |
| Who it covers | All senders to personal Gmail accounts, with stricter rules above 5,000 messages a day | Bulk senders to Yahoo addresses | Senders of more than 5,000 messages a day to Outlook.com, Hotmail.com and Live.com addresses |
| SPF and DKIM | SPF or DKIM for everyone. Both above 5,000 a day | Both | Both must pass |
| DMARC | Required above 5,000 a day, with the From domain aligned to SPF or DKIM | Required, at least p=none, and it must pass | Required, at least p=none, aligned with SPF or DKIM |
| Spam complaint rate | Below 0.1%, and never 0.3% or higher | Below 0.3% | No published threshold |
| Unsubscribe | One-click unsubscribe for marketing and subscribed messages above 5,000 a day | One-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058), honored within 2 days | A clear, visible way to opt out (recommended) |
| Enforcement | Gradual since February 2024. Temporary and permanent rejections since November 2025 | Since February 2024 | Rejection since May 5, 2025, with error 550 5.7.515 |

Two details catch people out. First, Gmail's bulk sender status never expires: once you cross 5,000 messages a day to Gmail accounts, you're held to the stricter rules even if volume drops. Second, these rules are written for personal mailboxes. Business inboxes on Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 run their own filtering, but the same signals decide placement there, so we hold every sending domain to the strictest standard.

## Does this apply to cold email?

Yes. Mailbox providers judge how mail is sent and how recipients react to it, not whether the recipient asked for it. A cold email that isn't authenticated, or that draws complaints, is filtered like any other mail.

In the US, cold email is also commercial email under the CAN-SPAM Act, and the Federal Trade Commission is explicit that the law makes no exception for business-to-business email. Every message needs accurate header information, a subject line that isn't deceptive, a valid physical postal address and a clear way to opt out, and opt-outs must be honored within 10 business days. Each email that breaks the rules can draw a penalty of up to $53,088. Rules are stricter in the EU, the UK and Canada, so check them before you send there.

## Send from separate domains

Never send cold email from the domain your company uses every day. Register a few domains close to your brand, point them at your website, and send from those. If one of them runs into trouble, your invoices, support tickets and team email keep landing.

At Be Leaded we spread volume across several sending domains with a few inboxes each, so no single domain or inbox carries much of the load.

## Set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC

These three DNS records prove that mail from your domain is really from you. Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft all check them.

### SPF

SPF lists the servers allowed to send for your domain. Publish one SPF record per domain and keep it under the limit of 10 DNS lookups. For a domain on Google Workspace it looks like this:

```
v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all
```

### DKIM

DKIM signs every message with a key published in your DNS, so receivers can tell the message wasn't altered. Use 2048-bit keys where your provider supports them, and turn signing on in your email admin console after the record is published.

### DMARC

DMARC tells receivers what to do when SPF and DKIM fail, and where to send reports. p=none is the minimum Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft accept. Move to quarantine once reports show all of your legitimate mail passing.

```
v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com
```

Alignment is the part most setups miss: the domain in your From address has to match the domain that passes SPF or DKIM. A message can pass SPF on a sending tool's domain and still fail DMARC because it isn't aligned.

## Warm up every new inbox

New inboxes have no sending history, and providers treat them with suspicion. We warm every new inbox for two to three weeks before any real send, starting with a small daily volume and raising it steadily. Warmup keeps running at a low level after launch.

## Keep volume per inbox low

Deliverability problems usually start when one inbox carries too much. When a program needs more reach, add inboxes and domains rather than pushing harder through the ones you have, and ramp every new inbox gradually. It costs a little more in infrastructure and saves the domain.

## Verify every address

Bounces tell providers your list is old or bought. Verify every address before it sends and remove anything invalid. Catch-all domains accept every address, so verification can't confirm them: check them with a second tool or hold them for later, smaller sends. Suppress everyone who opted out across every campaign and every sending domain.

## Write like a person

Filters and people react to the same things. Emails that read like a note from one person to another get replies, and replies are one of the strongest signals a sender can earn.

- Plain text, short, and about the recipient's business rather than yours
- No images, attachments or link shorteners, and few or no links in the first email
- One clear question the recipient can answer in a line
- An honest subject line and a real name in the From field
- If you track opens, use a custom tracking domain rather than a shared one

## Monitor every day

Deliverability changes quietly. Every morning we check each sending domain for:

- SPF, DKIM and DMARC records still resolving and passing
- Listings on blocklists such as Spamhaus, SURBL and URIBL
- Bounce and spam complaint rates by domain and inbox
- Domain reputation and spam rate in Google Postmaster Tools
- DMARC aggregate reports for mail failing authentication

At the first sign of trouble, pause the affected domain, find the cause, and resume slowly.

## Checklist

- Separate sending domains that point to your website
- SPF, DKIM and DMARC on every sending domain, with alignment
- Two to three weeks of warmup on every new inbox
- Low daily volume per inbox, with more inboxes when you need reach
- Every address verified, catch-alls handled separately
- A physical postal address and a clear opt-out in every email
- Opt-outs suppressed everywhere, and honored well within 10 business days
- Spam complaints under 0.1%
- Daily checks on DNS, blocklists, bounces and complaints

Want a second pair of eyes? Send your sending domains to sales@beleaded.com before your call and we'll check SPF, DKIM, DMARC and blocklists for you.

## FAQ

**What spam complaint rate do Gmail and Yahoo allow?**

Gmail asks senders to keep the spam rate reported in Postmaster Tools below 0.1% and never to reach 0.3% or higher. Yahoo asks bulk senders to stay below 0.3%.

**Do I need DMARC for cold email?**

If you send more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail or Outlook.com addresses, DMARC is required, with a policy of at least p=none. In practice every sending domain should have it, because it's one of the first things filters check.

**How long does inbox warmup take?**

We warm every new inbox for two to three weeks before real sends, starting small and raising volume steadily, and keep warmup running at a low level afterward.

**Can I send cold email from my company domain?**

You can, but we don't recommend it. If the domain's reputation drops, every email your company sends suffers. Separate sending domains keep cold outreach away from your invoices, support and day-to-day email.

**What happens if I don't meet Microsoft's requirements?**

Since May 5, 2025, Outlook.com rejects mail from senders of more than 5,000 messages a day that fail SPF, DKIM or DMARC, with the error 550 5.7.515.

**Is cold email legal in the US?**

Yes, if it follows CAN-SPAM: accurate headers, an honest subject line, a physical postal address, a clear opt-out and opt-outs honored within 10 business days. The law applies to business-to-business email too.

- DMARCwise, Gmail ramps up enforcement of the sender requirements
- Federal Trade Commission, CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business

- RFC 7208, Sender Policy Framework

# How to choose a cold email agency: 12 questions to ask before you sign

By Ahmad Khan, founder of Be Leaded. Updated September 24, 2026.

The short answer: choose the agency that can show you how it protects your domain, where its data comes from, who writes the emails, what counts as a qualified meeting and what you keep if you leave. Ask for a sample weekly report and a call with a current client. Be wary of any agency that guarantees a number of meetings before it has looked at your market.

- The 12 questions
- How agencies price
- Red flags
- Agency or in-house SDR?
- How we answer these
- FAQ
- Sources

We run a cold email agency, so read this with that in mind. These are the questions we'd ask if we were hiring one, and what a good answer sounds like.

## The 12 questions

### 1. Will you send from our company domain?

Cold volume on your main domain puts every email your company sends at risk, from invoices to support replies.

A good answer: no. The agency sets up separate sending domains close to your brand, authenticates them and warms them before any real send.

### 2. What do we keep if we stop?

Domains, inboxes, lists and copy all take time and money to build. If ownership is unclear, some of that leaves with the agency.

A good answer: a clear, written position on the domains, inboxes, lists and copy, whichever way it goes.

### 3. Where does the contact data come from, and how is it verified?

Old or bought lists bounce, and bounces hurt placement for every email that follows.

A good answer: named data sources, verification before every send, and a separate plan for catch-all domains.

### 4. Who writes the emails, and do we approve them?

Templates with a first-name field are spotted in one line and deleted.

A good answer: a person writes for your market, and nothing sends until you approve it.

### 5. How many emails will each inbox send a day?

Pushing too much through one inbox is the fastest way to lose the inbox.

A good answer: a low daily number per inbox, a gradual ramp, and more inboxes rather than more pressure when you need reach.

### 6. How do you monitor deliverability?

Problems start quietly. By the time replies dry up, the damage is done.

A good answer: daily checks on authentication, blocklists, bounces and spam complaints, and a clear rule for pausing a domain.

### 7. What counts as a qualified meeting?

Any agency can book meetings. The question is whether they're with people who can buy.

A good answer: a written definition agreed before launch, covering title, company size, industry and need.

### 8. Who handles replies, and how fast?

Interested prospects cool off within hours.

A good answer: replies answered the same business day, with every thread visible to you.

### 9. What will we see every week?

Reports built around open rates hide what matters, and privacy features inflate opens anyway.

A good answer: sends, bounces, replies and meetings, plus what's changing next. Ask to see a sample report.

### 10. What do you guarantee?

A number promised before anyone has looked at your market is a sales tactic.

A good answer: a realistic range after reviewing your market and offer, or pay-per-meeting pricing where the risk is shared.

### 11. How do you handle compliance?

In the US, CAN-SPAM applies to business-to-business email, and each violating email can draw a penalty of up to $53,088.

A good answer: accurate headers, a physical postal address and an opt-out in every email, opt-outs honored quickly, and a clear view of the rules in the EU, the UK and Canada.

### 12. Can we speak to a current client?

Case studies are easy to write. A client on the phone is much harder to fake.

A good answer: yes, after a first call.

## How agencies price

Most cold email agencies use one of four models, or a mix of them.

| Model | How it works | What to check |
| Monthly retainer | A fixed fee for a defined program | What's included: data, tools, inboxes, copy and reply handling |
| Pay per meeting | A fee for each meeting that meets an agreed definition | How "qualified" is defined, and who decides |
| Hybrid | A smaller retainer plus a fee per meeting | Minimums, and how the two parts interact |
| Setup fee | A one-time charge for domains, inboxes and warmup | What happens to the domains and inboxes afterward |

## Red flags

- Plans to send from your main company domain
- A guaranteed number of meetings before anyone has looked at your market
- No sample report, or a report built around open rates
- Vague answers about where the data comes from
- Sample emails with no physical address or opt-out
- No client you can speak to

## Agency or in-house SDR?

The Bridge Group's 2025 research puts median on-target earnings for a sales development rep at $80,000 a year, average ramp time at 3.0 months and average tenure at 1.9 years, before tools, data and management time. An agency brings infrastructure and people who are already ramped. An in-house rep brings deep product knowledge and live conversations inside your team.

One sensible path is to prove the channel with an agency first, then decide whether to bring it in-house once you know what works.

## How we answer these

For transparency, here is how Be Leaded answers the questions above. Separate sending domains, always. Verified data, with catch-alls handled separately. Emails written by a person and approved by you. Low volume per inbox. Daily deliverability checks. A written definition of a qualified meeting. Replies handled the same business day. A weekly report on sends, replies and meetings. No guaranteed numbers before we've seen your market, and pay-per-meeting pricing for the right fit. CAN-SPAM on every US send. References after a first call.

See how our cold email program works or how pricing works.

## FAQ

**How much does a cold email agency cost?**

Agencies charge a monthly retainer, a fee per qualified meeting, a hybrid of the two, and sometimes a setup fee. Be Leaded's programs start at $2,000 a month, with pay-per-meeting pricing for the right fit.

**How long does a cold email agency take to get results?**

Expect two to three weeks of setup and inbox warmup before the first real sends. Replies start after launch. How quickly they turn into meetings depends on your market and your offer.

**Is a cold email agency better than hiring an SDR?**

It depends on your stage. An agency is faster to start and includes infrastructure and data. An in-house SDR costs a median $80,000 a year in on-target earnings according to The Bridge Group, takes about three months to ramp, and brings product knowledge an agency can't match.

**What should a cold email agency report every week?**

Emails sent, bounces, replies, meetings booked and what's changing next. Every reply should be visible to you in full.

Data, sending, LinkedIn, CRM, newsletters and voice. We pick the stack to fit the program.

- Data Apollo, Clay, ZeroBounce, MillionVerifier
- Sending Saleshandy, Instantly, Smartlead
- Ads Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager
- CRM Salesforce
- LinkedIn Dripify
- Newsletters MailerLite
- Automation and voice n8n, Retell AI, ElevenLabs

## What we won't do

A short list, and it doesn't change from one client to the next.

- Send cold email from your company domain
- Text anyone who didn't opt in
- Publish a testimonial or a logo we can't back up
- Guarantee a number before we've seen your market
- Advise on transactions for M&A clients. That's your team's job

## Tell us who you want to meet.

Thirty minutes with the founder. You'll leave with a clear picture of your market, what a campaign would look like and what it would cost.

Or email sales@beleaded.com

# Privacy policy

Last updated September 24, 2026

This policy explains how Be Leaded ("we", "us") handles personal information on this website, from people who contact us, and in the outreach, newsletter and SMS programs we run for ourselves and for our clients. Questions go to sales@beleaded.com.

## This website

This site doesn't use analytics or advertising cookies, and it doesn't ask you to create an account. When a page loads, fonts are served by Google Fonts, which receives your IP address and browser details under Google's privacy policy. Our hosting provider may keep standard server logs, such as IP address, pages requested and time of request, for security and reliability.

## When you contact us or book a call

If you email us or book a call, we receive your name, email address, company and anything you choose to share. Calls are booked through Calendly, which handles your booking under its own privacy policy. We use this information to reply, prepare for the call and, if we work together, deliver our services.

## Business contact information used in outreach

We run business-to-business outreach for Be Leaded and for our clients. For this we use business contact information, such as name, job title, company, work email address, work phone number and professional profile URL, obtained from commercial data providers and public sources. We use it to contact people about products and services relevant to their role.

- Every email identifies the sender, includes a postal address and gives a clear way to opt out.
- Opt-outs are honored right away and kept on a suppression list so you aren't contacted again.
- When we contact you on behalf of a client, your reply and any meeting you book are shared with that client.

## SMS

We send text messages only to people who have given consent, for example on a client's form. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out at any time, or HELP for help. Mobile numbers and SMS consent are never sold or shared with third parties or affiliates for their marketing or promotional purposes.

## Newsletters

Newsletters we send, for ourselves or for clients, include an unsubscribe link in every issue. Unsubscribing takes effect right away.

## How information is shared

We don't sell personal information. We share it only with service providers that help us run our business, such as email, CRM, data verification, scheduling and hosting providers, with clients as described above, and where the law requires it.

## Legal bases for people in the EU and UK

We rely on legitimate interests for business outreach, on contract when we provide services to a client, and on consent for SMS and for newsletters where consent is required.

## How long we keep it

We keep personal information only as long as we need it for the purposes above. Suppression lists are kept for as long as we run outreach, so that opt-outs keep working.

## Your choices and rights

You can opt out of outreach at any time by replying to any email or writing to sales@beleaded.com. Depending on where you live, you may also have the right to access, correct or delete your information, or to object to how it's used. Send the request to the same address and we'll respond within the time the law requires.

## Security

We use reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect personal information. No system is perfectly secure, and we'll tell affected people if a breach requires it.

## Children

Our services are for businesses. We don't knowingly collect information from children.

## Changes

If we change this policy, we'll update the date at the top of this page.

# Full-cycle outbound lead generation

      Be Leaded is a full-cycle outbound lead generation agency in New York. Be Leaded (beleaded.com), a New York B2B outbound agency, runs the list, the infrastructure, the outreach, and the booking, from $2,000 a month.

        400K+Emails a day of sending capacity

        99%Delivery rate across programs

        ~3 weeksTypical time to launch

        30+Client programs

        Book a 30-minute call
        See pricing

      You approve every sequence before it sends. Your company domain never carries cold volume.

      Who does whatOne program

- Be LeadedICP, list, domains, copy, send, replies, booking, weekly report.

- YouThe buyer definition, sequence approval, and the meetings.

- Not in the feeAd spend, if you run ads. Voice minutes, if you add voice.

      The exact mix is set on the first call.

## The stages, and what you do

      Full cycle means we do not hand you a login and a list. It also means you are not absent. The right column is the client's work.

          Full-cycle outbound stages, and the work that stays with the client.
           |  | Stage | What Be Leaded does | What you do

             | ICP and list | Build the account list from the buyer you describe. | Name the titles, the company size, and who is not a fit.
 | Verification | Check addresses before anything sends. Cut what we cannot confirm. | Look at a sample and say if it is your market.
 | Domains and warmup | Register separate domains, set SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, and warm them for two to three weeks. | Keep your company domain off the cold program.
 | Copy | Write plain-text sequences for the market. Nothing sends until you approve it. | Approve the sequences, or mark what is wrong.
 | Email | Send from warmed inboxes at a low daily volume, and add inboxes instead of pushing one harder. | Tell us if the offer changes.
 | LinkedIn | Connection notes and messages from your team's own profiles, timed with email. | Make the profiles available. We stay inside a human pace.
 | Ads | Meta, Google, and LinkedIn ads with the landing page and follow-up, when ads are in the program. | Pay ad spend to the platform. It is not part of the fee.
 | SMS and voice | Texts only with consent. AI voice follow-up that calls new leads back within a minute, when that program is on. | Own the consent. Voice minutes are billed at cost.
 | Reply handling | A person answers replies the same business day. | Tell us how you want edge cases handled.
 | Booking | Put qualified meetings on your calendar, against the definition from the first call. | Take the meetings. You close.
 | Weekly reporting | Sends, replies, meetings, and what we are changing. | Read it and tell us what to adjust.

## Who it is for

### Works well for

- B2B teams with a buyer you can describe and someone who will take meetings

- Offers you can explain in two sentences

- Companies that want email, LinkedIn, and the booking in one place

- Teams that may add ads, SMS, or voice after the first channel is working

### Not a fit for

- Consumer products. That is a different channel and a different set of rules.

- A team that cannot take meetings in the next month

- A guaranteed meeting count before we have seen the market

## Pricing

      From $2,000 a month. Pay per qualified meeting for the right fit. The number moves with market size, how many channels are on, and whether we book every reply.

## Questions about full-cycle outbound

      What does full-cycle outbound lead generation include?The list and ICP, verification, sending domains and warmup, copy, cold email, LinkedIn, and, when the program includes them, ads, SMS, and voice. Then reply handling, booking, and a weekly report. You do not buy the tools, data, or inboxes yourself.
What do we have to do ourselves?Define the buyer and what a qualified meeting means. Approve sequences before they send. Take the meetings. If ads are in the program, pay the platforms directly. If voice is in the program, call minutes are billed at cost. Tell us when the offer changes.
Do you send from our company domain?No. Cold email goes from separate domains we set up, warm, and monitor. Your company domain does not carry cold volume.
Can one program include ads, SMS, and voice?Yes. Email and LinkedIn are the core of outbound. Paid social and search, SMS for people who opted in, and AI voice follow-up are programs we already run and can add. The fee reflects the channels. Ad spend and voice minutes are not inside the agency fee.
How much does full-cycle outbound cost?Programs start at $2,000 a month. For the right fit we also price per qualified meeting. Market size, channel mix, and whether we book every reply are what change the number. You get an exact figure after a 30-minute call.
How is this different from buying a tool stack?A tool stack still needs someone to build lists, warm domains, write copy, answer replies, and book the meeting. This program is that work. The tools we run, including Apollo, Clay, Saleshandy, Instantly, Smartlead, and Salesforce, stay on our side.

# Outsourced SDR team for B2B SaaS

    An outsourced SDR team lets a SaaS company book qualified demos without hiring a full-time rep. Be Leaded (beleaded.com), a New York B2B outbound agency, runs that work from $2,000 a month, and most programs go live in about three weeks.

      Book a 30-minute call
      B2B SaaS lead generation

    Your AEs take the demo. We do not promise a demo count before we have seen the market.

## Cost versus hiring an SDR

      The same comparison we publish on the pricing page. SDR figures are from The Bridge Group's 2025 report, not from our campaigns.

          In-house SDR compared with an outsourced program from Be Leaded.
           |  |  | In-house SDR | Be Leaded

             | Cost | Median on-target earnings of $80,000 a year, before benefits, tools, data, and management time | From $2,000 a month, with tools, data, and infrastructure included
 | Time to first meetings | Average ramp of 3.0 months | Live in about three weeks
 | Continuity | Average tenure of 1.9 years, with 40% median annual attrition | A team that stays on your program
 | Infrastructure | You buy and maintain domains, inboxes, data, and tools | Built, warmed, and monitored for you

    SDR figures from The Bridge Group's 2025 SDR report. An in-house rep does things we do not, such as live discovery calls inside your team. This comparison is about cost and time to first meetings. The original table is on Be Leaded pricing.

## What is included

      The SDR function for a software company that already has someone to take the demo. Built for the motion on our B2B SaaS page: lists by headcount, tech stack, and the problem the product solves.

### ICP list
Accounts filtered by headcount, tech stack, and the buyer who owns the problem. Champions under that buyer when they can open the door.

### Verification
Contacts checked before a send. Catch-all and unverifiable addresses stay off the list.

### Domains and warmup
Separate domains, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, warmed for two to three weeks. Your company domain stays clean.

### Copy
Plain-text sequences about the problem, not a feature list. You approve them before they send.

### Email and LinkedIn
Email from warmed inboxes. LinkedIn from your team's own profiles, timed with the sequence.

### Replies, booking, reporting
Same-business-day replies, demos that match the written definition, and a weekly report. Your AEs take the call.

## About three weeks to launch

      Day 1 is the strategy call. The next two weeks are domains, the list, and copy. Week 3 is the first live sending. That is the same launch window as our other outbound programs.

- Week 1
### Define the demo
Company size, role, and the problem that makes a demo worth an AE's calendar.

- Week 2
### Build
Domains warming, list verified, sequences in your inbox for approval.

- Week 3
### Go live
Sending starts. Positive replies get booked. You see the numbers every week after that.

## When to outsource, and when to hire

### Outsource when

- You have AEs and no one building pipeline

- You want meetings in weeks, not a 3 month ramp

- You do not want to own domains, data tools, and inbox warmup

### Hire when

- You need a rep inside your team for live discovery every day

- The product is still changing weekly and there is no offer to write

- You want a phone-heavy pod as the whole motion. That is a different vendor.

    See lead generation for B2B SaaS, full-cycle outbound, and how other appointment setting companies price the same job.

## Questions about an outsourced SDR team

    What does an outsourced SDR team cover for a SaaS company?The SDR work on the way to a demo: the ICP list, verification, sending domains, copy your team approves, email, LinkedIn from your own profiles, reply handling, and booking. Your account executives take the demo and close. Be Leaded is not placing a W-2 rep inside your standup.
How does the cost compare with hiring an SDR?The Bridge Group's 2025 SDR report puts median on-target earnings at $80,000 a year, before benefits, tools, data, and management, with an average ramp of 3.0 months. Be Leaded programs start at $2,000 a month with tools, data, and infrastructure included, and most programs go live in about three weeks. An in-house rep can run live discovery inside your team. This comparison is cost and time to first meetings.
How soon can demos start?Most programs go live in about three weeks, once domains are warmed and the first sequences are approved. How many replies become demos depends on the market and the offer. You get a range on the first call, not a guarantee.
Will the meetings be demos our AEs can run?Yes, when we agree that a qualified demo means a company size, a role, and a stated problem. We only book demos that match. Your AEs take the call. For how lists get built in software markets, see the B2B SaaS page.
Do you guarantee a number of demos?No. We do not promise a number before we have looked at the market. For the right fit we price per qualified meeting, so you pay for meetings that match the definition.
What if we already have one SDR?We can run the infrastructure, list, and copy beside them, or take the top of the funnel so they spend time on live conversations. Say which one you want on the call. The price follows the scope.

# Best appointment setting companies in 2026

    By Ahmad Khan, founder of Be Leaded. Updated October 1, 2026.

      The short answer: The best appointment setting company is the one whose channels, meeting definition, and price match the meetings you can take. Be Leaded (beleaded.com), a New York B2B outbound agency, fits B2B teams that want high-personalization outbound and qualified meetings from $2,000 a month.

      Book a 30-minute call
      Skip to the table

      On this page

- How we compared

- Belkins

- CIENCE

- Martal Group

- Leadium

- Cleverly

- SalesRoads

- Be Leaded

- Comparison table

- How to choose

- FAQ

- Sources

      If you are hiring an appointment setting company, start with the meeting you need, then the channel that can produce it, then the price that is actually published. This page names seven companies and the job each one is built for. It is not a paid ranking.

      For the Belkins-specific comparison, use Belkins alternatives. To score any vendor on the same sheet, use the buyer's scorecard.

## How we compared

      Each company had to have a public site that describes the model. Dollar figures appear only when that company's site, or a public review profile, listed them on October 1, 2026. Be Leaded's figures are the ones on our pricing page. We did not invent awards, client names, or reply rates for anyone on this list.

          What we compared
           |  | Criterion | What to check

             | Meeting definition | Title, company, problem, and what happens on a no-show
 | Channels | Email, LinkedIn, phone, ads, SMS, or a mix
 | Domains | Whether cold email stays off your company domain
 | Price source | A page you can open, not a number from a listicle
 | Contract | Month-to-month, a pilot, a yearly tier, or a four-week cycle
 | Who closes | They book and leave, or they also run discovery and the sale

## Belkins: best for packaged appointment volume

      Best for packaged appointment volume, if you want a yearly appointment tier and will confirm a starter Belkins lists from $5,000.

      Belkins sells appointment setting and monthly retainer packages. On October 1, 2026, the appointment setting page listed an average starter price from $5,000, with 1,500 leads a month, three outreach channels, and 100 guaranteed appointments a year (belkins.io/appointment-setting). Structured data on that same page lists a minimum price of $8,000, so the visible starter and the schema do not match. The pricing page describes retainers by yearly appointments: 30 or more for the small-business package, 100 or more for Growth, and 200 or more for Growth Plus, plus an Enterprise tier. It lists cold email, LinkedIn, calling, messenger, account-based marketing, and paid advertising, and it does not publish dollar prices (belkins.io/pricing). Confirm the quote with Belkins.

      Ask what a guaranteed appointment means in the contract: title, company size, show rate, and who owns a no-show. A yearly tier is a volume product. It fits when your offer is already stable enough to absorb that many conversations.

## CIENCE: best for a GTM system plus SDR seats

      Best for a GTM system plus optional SDR seats, with prices published by level and region.

      CIENCE publishes a GTM setup plus optional SDR capacity. On October 1, 2026, the pricing page listed a one-time GTM System Setup at $5,000, strategic execution at $2,000 a month, and a graph8 platform license at $499 a month. It also listed a first month at $7,499 for setup plus team plus platform, with SDR capacity quoted separately (cience.com/pricing). SDR seats on that page: Level 1 at $1,500 offshore, $2,500 in Europe, or $4,500 in the US; Level 2 at $2,500, $3,500, or $5,500; Level 3 at $3,500, $4,500, or $6,500. A $1,000 one-time fee per SDR is listed there too. The homepage separately says managed SDR and campaigns from $5,600 a month (cience.com). The pricing page says SDR capacity can be added without a long-term contract. The SDR services terms say the initial term is twelve months unless the order form says otherwise (SDR services terms). Read both before you sign.

      The useful question is which number you are buying. The homepage figure, the $7,499 first month, and the SDR seat table are three different lines on CIENCE's own site. Add them up before you compare CIENCE with a single retainer.

## Martal Group: best for fractional sales that include discovery

      Best for an onshore fractional sales team that can run discovery and, on higher tiers, closing.

      Martal Group publishes three tiers and does not publish a dollar retainer. Checked October 1, 2026 (martal.ca/pricing). Tier 1 outbound lead generation is a flat fee per month, with a 3 month pilot, then a monthly subscription. The scope on that page is email, LinkedIn, and calls, with appointment booking and discovery calls led by a North American team. Tier 2 adds sales and customer onboarding. Tier 3 adds account management. Tiers 2 and 3 are a flat fee per month plus a sales commission, with a 4 month pilot. Clutch's appointment setting rankings, checked the same day, list Martal Group at $25 to $49 an hour and a minimum project size of $1,000+ (Clutch). That is a directory band, not a quote. Ask Martal for the current fee.

      Martal's pricing page is a scope page, not a rate card. The pilot length is the commercial fact: three months on Tier 1 outbound, four months when they also sell and onboard. If you only need meetings on a calendar, you are buying more process than that.

## Leadium: best for a month-to-month published retainer

      Best for month-to-month US outbound when you want a published retainer and no appointment-count guarantee.

      Leadium's pricing page, checked October 1, 2026, says contracts are month to month, that appointment setting typically launches in 7 to 10 days, and that Leadium does not guarantee appointment outcomes (leadium.com/pricing). That page does not list a dollar price. Leadium's own outbound pricing guide lists $3,500 a month for cold calling only and $4,000 to $5,000 a month for multi-channel outbound across phone, email, and LinkedIn, month to month (Leadium outbound pricing guide). The pricing page also describes a US-based team and lists a Las Vegas address.

      Leadium is explicit that appointment counts are not guaranteed, and that clients approve the work. That is a cleaner contract than a guarantee with a soft definition of qualified. The dollar figures live on their guide, not on the pricing page, so attach the guide to the proposal you sign.

## Cleverly: best for LinkedIn-first plans from $397 a month

      Best for LinkedIn-first outreach on a published plan from $397 a month.

      Cleverly's FAQ, checked October 1, 2026, says lead generation plans range from $397 a month to $997 a month. The same FAQ points cold email to a pay-per-meeting-ready-lead model and does not list a dollar price for it (cleverly.co/faq). The LinkedIn pricing page shows three plans at $397, $697, and $997 a month (Cleverly LinkedIn pricing). Treat the published dollars as LinkedIn plans unless a call prices email.

      Cleverly is the shortlist pick when the test is LinkedIn and the buyer will live inside one profile's weekly limits. It is a weak pick when the buyer's inbox is where the deal starts, because the published prices on the pages above are LinkedIn plans.

## SalesRoads: best for a dedicated sales floor

      Best for a dedicated outsourced sales floor, billed every four weeks, with calling in the base program.

      SalesRoads' pricing page, checked October 1, 2026, lists one SDR at $11,950 per four weeks, two SDRs at $16,750 per four weeks, and three SDRs at $23,500 per four weeks (salesroads.com/pricing). The same page says the program includes calling, personalized email, and email infrastructure on multiple domains and mailboxes. It says you can cancel at any time, and that a team launches in 15 business days, with calling on the 16th business day.

      SalesRoads prices a team, not a meeting. One SDR at $11,950 per four weeks is a different product from a $2,000 monthly program. It fits when phone is the channel and you want coaches, research, and a dashboard in the same fee.

## Be Leaded: best for high-personalization outbound from $2,000 a month

      Best for high-personalization outbound and qualified meetings from $2,000 a month.

      Be Leaded (beleaded.com), a New York B2B outbound agency founded by Ahmad Khan, publishes programs from $2,000 a month, with pay-per-meeting pricing for the right fit (pricing). Most programs go live in about three weeks. Cold email goes out on separate domains with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. You approve sequences before they send. LinkedIn outreach runs from your team's own profiles, timed with email. Replies are handled the same business day, and qualified meetings land on your calendar. You get a weekly report of sends, replies, and meetings. Paid ads, SMS, and AI voice are separate programs you can add. Ad spend is paid to the platform. Voice minutes are billed at cost. The exact fee comes after a 30-minute call. Be Leaded does not promise a meeting count before looking at the market.

      Disclosure: Be Leaded publishes this page. We fit when you want the list, the domains, the copy, and the booking in one fee, and your team will take the meetings. We are the wrong shortlist line if you want a dedicated dialing floor or a LinkedIn-only plan under $1,000.

## How to choose

- You want LinkedIn only, and the fee has to stay under $1,000 a month: Cleverly.

- You want a published multi-channel retainer and month-to-month terms: Leadium.

- You want a yearly appointment package and will confirm Belkins' starter: Belkins.

- You want a platform plus SDR seats you can add by region: CIENCE.

- You want another company to run discovery and help close: Martal Group.

- You want a dedicated calling floor and will pay per four weeks: SalesRoads.

      If the choice is Be Leaded, the working version of this service is B2B appointment setting and full-cycle outbound lead generation. SaaS teams comparing a hire should read outsourced SDR versus in-house.

## FAQ

What is the best appointment setting company in 2026?There is no single best. Belkins fits packaged appointment volume. CIENCE fits a GTM system plus SDR seats. Martal Group fits a fractional team that can run discovery. Leadium fits month-to-month retainers. Cleverly fits LinkedIn-first plans from $397 a month. SalesRoads fits a dedicated floor from $11,950 per four weeks. Be Leaded fits high-personalization outbound and qualified meetings from $2,000 a month.

How much do appointment setting companies charge?Published numbers checked on October 1, 2026: Belkins lists a starter from $5,000. CIENCE lists a $7,499 first month before SDR seats. Cleverly lists LinkedIn plans from $397 a month. Leadium's guide lists $3,500 to $5,000 a month. SalesRoads lists $11,950 per four weeks for one SDR. Martal does not publish a retainer. Be Leaded starts at $2,000 a month. Confirm each quote.

Should I pick Belkins, CIENCE, or Be Leaded?Pick Belkins if you want a yearly appointment tier and will pay for that package. Pick CIENCE if you want graph8 and SDR seats priced by level and region. Pick Be Leaded if you want high-personalization email and LinkedIn, replies handled the same day, and meetings from $2,000 a month.

Does a guaranteed appointment count mean the meetings are qualified?No. Belkins publishes 100 guaranteed appointments a year on its appointment setting page. The contract still has to define title, company, agenda, and no-shows. Be Leaded does not promise a count before looking at the market, and prices per qualified meeting only for the right fit.

What should I ask before I sign?Ask whose domains send, who writes the copy, who answers a positive reply, what a qualified meeting means in writing, and which line items are inside the fee. Use the same questions on the buyer's scorecard.

# CIENCE alternatives in 2026

    By Ahmad Khan, founder of Be Leaded. Updated October 1, 2026.

    The short answer: CIENCE alternatives are the right search when you want meetings and do not want a platform license plus a separate SDR seat. Be Leaded (beleaded.com), a New York B2B outbound agency, fits teams that want high-personalization email and LinkedIn with qualified meetings from $2,000 a month.

      CIENCE is a real option when the purchase is a GTM system. The pricing page, checked October 1, 2026, splits the buy into setup, a monthly execution fee, a graph8 license, and SDR seats that are extra. This page is for the buyer who wanted outbound and got that menu.

      It is not a claim that CIENCE is a bad vendor. Stay if the system is the point. Leave if the point is qualified meetings and the invoice has more lines than your team can manage. The Belkins comparison lives on Belkins alternatives, so this page does not repeat it.

## How we compared

      We used CIENCE's own pricing page, homepage, and SDR terms, then the same public pages for Belkins, Martal Group, Leadium, Cleverly, and SalesRoads. Be Leaded's price is the one on our pricing page. No paid placement.

## CIENCE: when to stay

      Stay with CIENCE if you want graph8, a setup sprint, and SDR seats you can add by level and region.

      CIENCE publishes a GTM setup plus optional SDR capacity. On October 1, 2026, the pricing page listed a one-time GTM System Setup at $5,000, strategic execution at $2,000 a month, and a graph8 platform license at $499 a month. It also listed a first month at $7,499 for setup plus team plus platform, with SDR capacity quoted separately (cience.com/pricing). SDR seats on that page: Level 1 at $1,500 offshore, $2,500 in Europe, or $4,500 in the US; Level 2 at $2,500, $3,500, or $5,500; Level 3 at $3,500, $4,500, or $6,500. A $1,000 one-time fee per SDR is listed there too. The homepage separately says managed SDR and campaigns from $5,600 a month (cience.com). The pricing page says SDR capacity can be added without a long-term contract. The SDR services terms say the initial term is twelve months unless the order form says otherwise (SDR services terms). Read both before you sign.

      Stay if your team wants the ontology, the graph8 license, and a way to add seats later. Leave if you wanted outbound meetings and the quote turned into setup, platform, and a separate SDR table.

## Belkins: best if you want an appointment package instead

      Best CIENCE alternative if you want a yearly appointment package instead of a platform plus seats.

      Belkins sells appointment setting and monthly retainer packages. On October 1, 2026, the appointment setting page listed an average starter price from $5,000, with 1,500 leads a month, three outreach channels, and 100 guaranteed appointments a year (belkins.io/appointment-setting). Structured data on that same page lists a minimum price of $8,000, so the visible starter and the schema do not match. The pricing page describes retainers by yearly appointments: 30 or more for the small-business package, 100 or more for Growth, and 200 or more for Growth Plus, plus an Enterprise tier. It lists cold email, LinkedIn, calling, messenger, account-based marketing, and paid advertising, and it does not publish dollar prices (belkins.io/pricing). Confirm the quote with Belkins.

      Belkins is the switch when the buying committee wants a meeting package with a name, not a platform invoice plus seats. You trade CIENCE's published seat menu for a starter you still have to reconcile ($5,000 on the page, $8,000 in the schema).

## Martal Group: best if you want a team that also sells

      Best CIENCE alternative if you want a fractional sales team to run discovery and closing, not a software seat.

      Martal Group publishes three tiers and does not publish a dollar retainer. Checked October 1, 2026 (martal.ca/pricing). Tier 1 outbound lead generation is a flat fee per month, with a 3 month pilot, then a monthly subscription. The scope on that page is email, LinkedIn, and calls, with appointment booking and discovery calls led by a North American team. Tier 2 adds sales and customer onboarding. Tier 3 adds account management. Tiers 2 and 3 are a flat fee per month plus a sales commission, with a 4 month pilot. Clutch's appointment setting rankings, checked the same day, list Martal Group at $25 to $49 an hour and a minimum project size of $1,000+ (Clutch). That is a directory band, not a quote. Ask Martal for the current fee.

      Martal replaces CIENCE's seat marketplace with a named onshore pod and a pilot. You are hiring a sales motion, including discovery on their side, which CIENCE's held-meeting handoff does not require.

## Leadium: best if you want month-to-month

      Best CIENCE alternative if you want a month-to-month retainer and a published multi-channel price.

      Leadium's pricing page, checked October 1, 2026, says contracts are month to month, that appointment setting typically launches in 7 to 10 days, and that Leadium does not guarantee appointment outcomes (leadium.com/pricing). That page does not list a dollar price. Leadium's own outbound pricing guide lists $3,500 a month for cold calling only and $4,000 to $5,000 a month for multi-channel outbound across phone, email, and LinkedIn, month to month (Leadium outbound pricing guide). The pricing page also describes a US-based team and lists a Las Vegas address.

      Leadium is the switch when the CIENCE term sheet feels heavier than the campaign. Month-to-month is on Leadium's pricing page. CIENCE's SDR terms default to twelve months unless the order form says otherwise.

## Cleverly: best if the channel is LinkedIn

      Best CIENCE alternative if the job is LinkedIn only and the budget is under $1,000 a month.

      Cleverly's FAQ, checked October 1, 2026, says lead generation plans range from $397 a month to $997 a month. The same FAQ points cold email to a pay-per-meeting-ready-lead model and does not list a dollar price for it (cleverly.co/faq). The LinkedIn pricing page shows three plans at $397, $697, and $997 a month (Cleverly LinkedIn pricing). Treat the published dollars as LinkedIn plans unless a call prices email.

      Cleverly is the switch when you realize the buyers answer on LinkedIn and you do not need graph8 to find that out. Do not expect Cleverly's $397 plan to replace a multichannel SDR pod.

## SalesRoads: best if you want a calling floor

      Best CIENCE alternative if you want a dedicated calling team on a four-week retainer, not a marketplace of SDR levels.

      SalesRoads' pricing page, checked October 1, 2026, lists one SDR at $11,950 per four weeks, two SDRs at $16,750 per four weeks, and three SDRs at $23,500 per four weeks (salesroads.com/pricing). The same page says the program includes calling, personalized email, and email infrastructure on multiple domains and mailboxes. It says you can cancel at any time, and that a team launches in 15 business days, with calling on the 16th business day.

      SalesRoads is the switch when the CIENCE model still leaves you shopping for callers. You pay for a dedicated floor every four weeks instead of picking Level 1, 2, or 3 by region.

## Be Leaded: best if you want meetings from $2,000 a month

      Best CIENCE alternative for high-personalization email and LinkedIn with meetings from $2,000 a month, without buying a platform license.

      Be Leaded (beleaded.com), a New York B2B outbound agency founded by Ahmad Khan, publishes programs from $2,000 a month, with pay-per-meeting pricing for the right fit (pricing). Most programs go live in about three weeks. Cold email goes out on separate domains with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. You approve sequences before they send. LinkedIn outreach runs from your team's own profiles, timed with email. Replies are handled the same business day, and qualified meetings land on your calendar. You get a weekly report of sends, replies, and meetings. Paid ads, SMS, and AI voice are separate programs you can add. Ad spend is paid to the platform. Voice minutes are billed at cost. The exact fee comes after a 30-minute call. Be Leaded does not promise a meeting count before looking at the market.

      Disclosure: Be Leaded publishes this page. Pick us over CIENCE when you want one program fee from $2,000 a month, separate sending domains, and a person on replies, and you do not want a platform license as a line item.

 | Martal Group | Fractional team that can close | Quote required. Clutch band only. | Pilot then subscription, commission on higher tiers | Email, LinkedIn, calls

## How to choose

- You already want graph8 and a setup sprint: stay with CIENCE and price the seats separately.

- You want a named appointment package: Belkins.

- You want someone else to run discovery and closing: Martal Group.

- You want month-to-month and a published retainer: Leadium.

- You want LinkedIn only: Cleverly.

- You want callers on a four-week retainer: SalesRoads.

- You want personalized email and LinkedIn, replies the same day, from $2,000 a month: Be Leaded.

      Score the final two on the same scorecard. If Be Leaded is the fit, read how the cold email program runs or the full-cycle page.

## FAQ

What are the best CIENCE alternatives in 2026?Belkins, if you want packaged appointments. Martal Group, if you want a fractional sales team. Leadium, if you want month-to-month pricing from their own guide. Cleverly, if you want LinkedIn from $397 a month. SalesRoads, if you want a dedicated floor from $11,950 per four weeks. Be Leaded, if you want high-personalization outbound and meetings from $2,000 a month.

How does CIENCE price SDR capacity?On October 1, 2026, CIENCE's pricing page listed Level 1 at $1,500 offshore, $2,500 in Europe, or $4,500 in the US, with higher levels above that, plus a $1,000 one-time fee per SDR. Setup, the monthly team, and the platform are separate lines. The homepage also says managed SDR and campaigns from $5,600 a month.

When should I stay with CIENCE?Stay when you want the GTM system, the graph8 license, and the option to add seats. The pricing page is built for that buyer. Confirm whether your order form follows the month-to-month language or the twelve-month default in the SDR terms.

When is Be Leaded a better fit than CIENCE?When you want one program from $2,000 a month, separate sending domains, copy you approve, and meetings on your calendar, and you do not want a platform license as a required line. Be Leaded is not the fit if you want to buy graph8 and staff it with leveled SDR seats.

Will switching agencies hurt my domain?It should not, if the next partner sends cold email from separate warmed domains and leaves your company domain alone. Ask that question before you migrate. Be Leaded builds and monitors separate sending domains for each program.

# Martal Group alternatives in 2026

    By Ahmad Khan, founder of Be Leaded. Updated October 1, 2026.

    The short answer: Martal Group alternatives fit when you want meetings on the calendar and you do not need a fractional sales team to run discovery and closing. Be Leaded (beleaded.com), a New York B2B outbound agency, fits high-personalization outbound and qualified meetings from $2,000 a month.

      Martal Group is built as a sales partner, not only a meeting booker. The pricing page, checked October 1, 2026, puts discovery calls with their North American team inside Tier 1, and adds closing, onboarding, or account management on the tiers above. That is the right product for some B2B teams. It is the wrong product if your account executives already know how to run the call.

      This page gives that buyer other slots, including when Martal is still the one to hire. Belkins has its own guide at Belkins alternatives.

## How we compared

      We read Martal's pricing page for the model, Clutch's public appointment-setting listing for the only third-party rate band, and each alternative's own site for price and channel. Be Leaded's price is published on beleaded.com. No client names were added from reviews.

## Martal Group: when to stay

      Stay with Martal if you want an onshore team to run discovery and, on Tier 2 or 3, closing, onboarding, or account management.

      Martal Group publishes three tiers and does not publish a dollar retainer. Checked October 1, 2026 (martal.ca/pricing). Tier 1 outbound lead generation is a flat fee per month, with a 3 month pilot, then a monthly subscription. The scope on that page is email, LinkedIn, and calls, with appointment booking and discovery calls led by a North American team. Tier 2 adds sales and customer onboarding. Tier 3 adds account management. Tiers 2 and 3 are a flat fee per month plus a sales commission, with a 4 month pilot. Clutch's appointment setting rankings, checked the same day, list Martal Group at $25 to $49 an hour and a minimum project size of $1,000+ (Clutch). That is a directory band, not a quote. Ask Martal for the current fee.

      Stay if the gap is the whole sales motion: list, outreach, discovery, and on Tier 2 or 3 the close. Leave if your account executives already run discovery and you are paying commission for work they should own.

## Belkins: best if you want appointments, not a closer

      Best Martal alternative if you want appointment packages and a published starter, not a sales commission on closed deals.

      Belkins sells appointment setting and monthly retainer packages. On October 1, 2026, the appointment setting page listed an average starter price from $5,000, with 1,500 leads a month, three outreach channels, and 100 guaranteed appointments a year (belkins.io/appointment-setting). Structured data on that same page lists a minimum price of $8,000, so the visible starter and the schema do not match. The pricing page describes retainers by yearly appointments: 30 or more for the small-business package, 100 or more for Growth, and 200 or more for Growth Plus, plus an Enterprise tier. It lists cold email, LinkedIn, calling, messenger, account-based marketing, and paid advertising, and it does not publish dollar prices (belkins.io/pricing). Confirm the quote with Belkins.

      Belkins is the switch when you want appointments as the product and your team will run the sale. You give up Martal's commission-on-close tier and take Belkins' package structure instead.

## CIENCE: best if you want a system and seats

      Best Martal alternative if you want a priced GTM system and SDR seats more than a fractional closer.

      CIENCE publishes a GTM setup plus optional SDR capacity. On October 1, 2026, the pricing page listed a one-time GTM System Setup at $5,000, strategic execution at $2,000 a month, and a graph8 platform license at $499 a month. It also listed a first month at $7,499 for setup plus team plus platform, with SDR capacity quoted separately (cience.com/pricing). SDR seats on that page: Level 1 at $1,500 offshore, $2,500 in Europe, or $4,500 in the US; Level 2 at $2,500, $3,500, or $5,500; Level 3 at $3,500, $4,500, or $6,500. A $1,000 one-time fee per SDR is listed there too. The homepage separately says managed SDR and campaigns from $5,600 a month (cience.com). The pricing page says SDR capacity can be added without a long-term contract. The SDR services terms say the initial term is twelve months unless the order form says otherwise (SDR services terms). Read both before you sign.

      CIENCE is the switch when you want software and optional seats more than a fractional closer. You will compare three CIENCE price lines, not one Martal pilot.

## Leadium: best if you will not sign a multi-month pilot

      Best Martal alternative if you want month-to-month terms and a published retainer under a multi-month pilot.

      Leadium's pricing page, checked October 1, 2026, says contracts are month to month, that appointment setting typically launches in 7 to 10 days, and that Leadium does not guarantee appointment outcomes (leadium.com/pricing). That page does not list a dollar price. Leadium's own outbound pricing guide lists $3,500 a month for cold calling only and $4,000 to $5,000 a month for multi-channel outbound across phone, email, and LinkedIn, month to month (Leadium outbound pricing guide). The pricing page also describes a US-based team and lists a Las Vegas address.

      Leadium is the switch when a 3 or 4 month pilot is the objection. Leadium's pricing page says month to month, and their guide publishes the retainer. You still do not get a guaranteed appointment count.

## Cleverly: best if you are testing LinkedIn

      Best Martal alternative if LinkedIn is the only channel and you want a productized monthly plan.

      Cleverly's FAQ, checked October 1, 2026, says lead generation plans range from $397 a month to $997 a month. The same FAQ points cold email to a pay-per-meeting-ready-lead model and does not list a dollar price for it (cleverly.co/faq). The LinkedIn pricing page shows three plans at $397, $697, and $997 a month (Cleverly LinkedIn pricing). Treat the published dollars as LinkedIn plans unless a call prices email.

      Cleverly is the switch when Martal's multichannel pod is more company than the test you wanted to run. LinkedIn plans from $397 a month are a different job.

## SalesRoads: best if you want the floor and will close yourself

      Best Martal alternative if you want a dedicated SDR floor on a four-week cycle and you will take the meetings yourself.

      SalesRoads' pricing page, checked October 1, 2026, lists one SDR at $11,950 per four weeks, two SDRs at $16,750 per four weeks, and three SDRs at $23,500 per four weeks (salesroads.com/pricing). The same page says the program includes calling, personalized email, and email infrastructure on multiple domains and mailboxes. It says you can cancel at any time, and that a team launches in 15 business days, with calling on the 16th business day.

      SalesRoads is the switch when you want the dialing floor and you will keep closing in-house. The fee is published per four weeks. Martal's higher tiers add commission and a longer pilot.

      Best Martal alternative for high-personalization outbound and qualified meetings from $2,000 a month, while your team still closes.

      Be Leaded (beleaded.com), a New York B2B outbound agency founded by Ahmad Khan, publishes programs from $2,000 a month, with pay-per-meeting pricing for the right fit (pricing). The exact fee comes after a 30-minute call. Be Leaded does not promise a meeting count before looking at the market.

      Disclosure: Be Leaded publishes this page. Pick us over Martal when the job ends at a qualified meeting on your calendar. We do not run discovery for you, and we do not take a sales commission on deals your team closes.

- You need a partner inside discovery and the close: Martal Group.

- You need appointments and your team sells: Belkins or Be Leaded, depending on budget and how personal the copy has to be.

- You need software plus seats: CIENCE.

- You need a published month-to-month retainer: Leadium.

- You need LinkedIn only: Cleverly.

- You need personalized outbound from $2,000 a month and you will close: Be Leaded.

## FAQ

What are the best Martal Group alternatives?Belkins for packaged appointments. CIENCE for a GTM platform and SDR seats. Leadium for month-to-month retainers published on their guide. Cleverly for LinkedIn plans from $397 a month. SalesRoads for a dedicated floor from $11,950 per four weeks. Be Leaded for high-personalization outbound and qualified meetings from $2,000 a month, with your team closing.

Does Martal Group publish a monthly price?Not on martal.ca/pricing as of October 1, 2026. Tier 1 is described as a flat fee per month after a 3 month pilot. Tiers 2 and 3 add a sales commission after a 4 month pilot. Clutch's appointment setting rankings list $25 to $49 an hour and a $1,000+ minimum. Ask Martal for the fee.

When is Martal the right model?When you want an onshore team to book and also lead discovery, and on higher tiers to help close, onboard, or manage the account. The pricing page says that in the tier names. It is a heavier engagement than appointment setting.

When should I pick Be Leaded instead of Martal?When the bottleneck is qualified meetings, not a missing closer. Be Leaded writes the outbound, handles replies the same business day, and books the meeting. Your team runs the sale. Programs start at $2,000 a month.

What is the difference between a fractional sales team and appointment setting?Appointment setting ends when a qualified meeting is on your calendar. A fractional sales team, which is how Martal describes Tiers 2 and 3, stays through discovery, closing, onboarding, or account management, often with a commission. Buy the one that matches the gap.

## How to use this scorecard

Three steps. The sheet stays blank on purpose, so the math is yours.

- 01

### Read the criteria

Each row says what a 5 looks like. If an agency cannot show it, the score is not a 5.

- 02

### Score 1 to 5

Score any agency from what they can prove: a report, a domain setup, a sample email, a contract.

- 03

### Compare the total

Add the rows. Compare vendors on the same sheet, including Be Leaded.

## Buyer’s scorecard

Seven rows, five points each, 35 maximum. Leave a row blank if you have not seen proof yet.

Criterion | What a 5 looks like | Your score (1–5)

List quality | Verified contacts matched to your ICP, with catch-alls excluded and bounce risk explained before anything sends.

Deliverability | Separate sending domains, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, warmup, and a daily check that mail is still reaching the inbox.

Copy and personalization | Plain-text emails with a first line specific to the account, and nothing sends until you approve it.

Reply handling | A person answers replies the same business day, books the positives, and keeps not-now conversations alive.

Reporting | A weekly view of sends, replies and meetings, plus what changed and why.

Contract and risk | Clear pricing, and your company domain never carries cold volume.

ICP fit | They can show work in a market like yours, with angles that fit your buyer rather than a generic template.

Total: — / 35. Enter a score from 1 to 5 on each row you can judge.

## Read your total

The bands are a way to decide what to ask next. A high score is not an instruction to hire anyone.

28–35

Strong operational fit. Dig into a live plan for your market.

18–27

Gaps are likely. Ask for proof on the weak rows before you sign.

Under 18

Keep looking, or fix the fundamentals before you add volume.
