# Cold email agency pricing: what $2,000 a month includes

A useful price names what is included, whose domain sends the mail, and how a qualified meeting is defined. Ours start at $2,000 a month. The exact number comes after a 30-minute call.

Book a 30-minute call (https://calendly.com/ahmad-beleaded/30min) See how pricing works (https://www.beleaded.com/pricing/) Read the scorecard (https://www.beleaded.com/guides/best-cold-email-agency/)

## What the fee should include

If domains, data, or reply handling are extra, the monthly number is not the real cost.

### Separate sending domains

Cold email goes out from domains set up for the program, with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. Your company domain does not carry that volume.

### Inboxes and warmup

Inboxes are warmed before real prospecting starts. Most programs go live in about three weeks.

### Lists and verification

Accounts and contacts matched to your buyer, verified before the first send. Catch-all and unverifiable addresses stay off the list.

### Copy you approve

Plain-text sequences written for your market. Nothing sends until you approve it.

### Reply handling

Replies are answered the same business day, and qualified meetings go on your calendar.

### Weekly reporting

Sends, replies, and meetings, plus what is changing next. You can read every reply.

## Two ways Be Leaded prices

Both use the same infrastructure. The full comparison, including hiring an SDR, is on the pricing page (https://www.beleaded.com/pricing/).

### Monthly program

From $2,000 a month. A defined program for a fixed fee when you want outbound running every week without hiring.

### Pay per qualified meeting

For the right fit. You pay for meetings that match a definition agreed in writing before launch. The price is set after we review your market.

### What changes the number

Market size and volume, which channels you run, how many offers and segments, and whether we book meetings or hand replies to your team. Ad spend and voice minutes are paid at cost, on top of the fee.

## Questions about cold email agency pricing

Use the buyer's scorecard (https://www.beleaded.com/guides/best-cold-email-agency/) to score contract and risk the same way you score deliverability.

How much does a cold email agency cost?

Agencies charge a monthly retainer, a fee per qualified meeting, a mix of the two, and sometimes a setup fee. Be Leaded programs start at $2,000 a month. You get an exact number after a 30-minute call.

What should the monthly fee include?

Sending domains and inboxes, warmup, list building and verification, sequences written for your market, reply handling, and weekly reporting. You should not have to buy the tools, data, or inboxes on top.

Will cold email run on our company domain?

It should not. Be Leaded sends from separate domains that we set up, warm, and monitor. Your company domain never carries cold volume.

Do you guarantee a number of meetings?

We do not promise a meeting count before we have looked at your market and your offer. For the right fit, pricing is per qualified meeting, using a definition agreed in writing before launch.

Why isn't there one public price?

The work depends on market size, channels, how many offers you run, and whether we book the meetings or hand replies to your team. A single sticker price would not match those programs.

By Ahmad Khan (https://www.beleaded.com/about/), founder of Be Leaded. Updated October 1, 2026.

The short answer: Belkins alternatives are worth a hard look when budget, channel mix, contract flexibility, or personalization depth don’t match Belkins’ mid-market appointment packages. Cleverly, CIENCE, Martal, Leadium, and Be Leaded each win for a different job—not a fake ranking.

If you searched Belkins alternatives, you already know the pattern: Belkins shows up on almost every cold email and appointment setting roundup. That is rational to question. This cold email agency comparison gives honest “best for” slots to Belkins, Cleverly, CIENCE, Martal, Leadium, and Be Leaded (https://www.beleaded.com/cold-email-agency/) —so you can see when Belkins is the fit and when another shop is.

Belkins earns its listicle presence with reviews, an appointment-setting brand, and mid-market/enterprise packaging. Searching Belkins alternatives still makes sense when budget, channel mix, contract flexibility, or personalization depth do not match that model—or when you want deeper account-level copy than a high-volume SDR process tends to deliver.

We shortlist founders, Heads of Sales or Growth, and RevOps who are comparing two to four vendors. Belkins wins for some buyers. Be Leaded wins when you want high-personalization DFY outbound and meetings from about $2,000 a month without enterprise packaging theater. No paid ranking. No invented awards. ## How we compared Belkins alternatives (methodology)

We scored fit the way a buyer should—not by logo count. Soft mention only: teams shopping best cold email agencies in 2026 still need a channel and contract match, not another Top-10 list. For the full choosing process, see choosing a cold email agency (https://www.beleaded.com/guides/choosing-a-cold-email-agency/).

Criterion | What “good” looks like

Meeting definition | Qualified ICP plus agenda, not raw dials or opens

Channels | Email, LinkedIn, phone, ads, SMS—matched to how your buyers actually respond

Deliverability / domains | Separate sending domains, authentication, warmup; your brand domain protected

Personalization depth | Account-true copy versus mail-merge templates

Pricing model | Retainer vs pay-per-meeting vs productized tiers; clear lock-in

Contract / flexibility | Month-to-month vs annual meeting packages

Reply handling | Same-day human replies vs ticketed SDR queues

Fit by company stage | SMB vs mid-market vs enterprise packaging

Competitor pricing below is labeled as public third-party ranges or typical bands reported in directories as of 2026. Confirm every number on a sales call. Be Leaded’s floor is published on Be Leaded pricing (https://www.beleaded.com/pricing/): programs from about $2,000 a month.

## Belkins: best for guaranteed appointment volume at mid-market+ budgets

Belkins is best for teams that want steady meeting volume, an appointment-setting-first story, and a vendor with broad brand recognition in mid-market and enterprise searches. If your ACV and pipeline plan can support a mid-to-high five-figure monthly program, Belkins is often on the shortlist for a reason.

Typical pricing band (third-party): often listed around $5,000–$15,000 a month. Reported ranges vary; confirm with Belkins.

Strengths: review volume, packaged meetings, clear appointment-setting positioning.

Tradeoffs: can feel heavy for SMB budgets or early offer validation; less “from $2,000” transparency than smaller DFY shops. Packaged meeting commitments also assume your offer and ICP are stable enough to absorb volume. If you are still validating messaging, a lighter program may teach you faster before you buy Belkins-scale capacity.

Fair close: if you need Belkins-class volume and you have the budget, talk to them—this page is not an argument against that fit.

For a deeper read on what retainers usually include, see our guide to cold email agency pricing (https://www.beleaded.com/guides/cold-email-agency-pricing/).

## Cleverly: best for LinkedIn-first outreach on a tight budget

Cleverly productizes LinkedIn outreach with published low entry tiers—often cited from about $397 a month for LinkedIn packages. That makes it a common Belkins vs Cleverly comparison when budget and channel are the main variables.

Strengths: transparent tiers, LinkedIn specialization, accessible for smaller teams testing outbound.

Tradeoffs: single-channel limits if your buyers live in email or if you need enterprise multi-touch cycles; LinkedIn volume caps are real. Pick Cleverly when a LinkedIn-only test is the job. Pick a multi-channel DFY shop when email deliverability, reply handling, and calendar booking matter as much as connection requests.

If LinkedIn is part of a broader mix, compare with a dedicated LinkedIn lead generation (https://www.beleaded.com/linkedin-lead-generation-agency/) program that times outreach with email.

## CIENCE: best for enterprise-scale SDR + data platform buyers

CIENCE sells a tech-enabled multichannel / SDR-as-a-service motion with a strong data-platform narrative. Belkins vs CIENCE usually comes down to packaging: appointment packages versus platform-plus-services scale.

Pricing: platform plus services; full-service engagements often land in the mid-to-high thousands per month on third-party bands. Confirm on a call.

Strengths: scale, data ops, enterprise reporting.

Tradeoffs: overkill for lean teams; more platform feel than boutique relationship. If you need an SDR army and a data stack under one roof, CIENCE belongs on the list. If you want a lean, personalized program without enterprise packaging theater, look elsewhere on this page.

## Martal Group: best for full-funnel / fractional sales partnership (esp. B2B tech)

Martal positions as a fractional sales / multi-channel partner—email, LinkedIn, phone, and a sales-team-extension model that fits B2B tech and SaaS motions.

Strengths: outbound plus process partnership; useful when you need more than calendar fills.

Tradeoffs: retainers often higher (directories commonly cite roughly $4,000–$10,000+); heavier engagement than “just book meetings.” Choose Martal when you want a fractional sales org. Choose a meeting-focused agency when the bottleneck is simply getting qualified conversations on the calendar.

## Leadium: best for flexible / month-to-month outbound programs

Leadium is often cited as a boutique-style DFY outbound shop with flexibility and month-to-month options as a differentiator versus annual meeting packages.

Pricing: low-to-mid thousands typical in directories. Confirm current packaging on a call.

Strengths: accountability via flexible contracts; emphasis on data validation.

Tradeoffs: not the “guaranteed yearly meetings” Belkins story. If contract flexibility is your top filter among Belkins competitors, Leadium earns a slot. Still press on meeting definition, domains, and reply SLA before you sign.

## Be Leaded: best for high-personalization outbound + meetings from ~$2,000/mo

Disclosure: Be Leaded publishes this guide. Here’s where we honestly fit.

Be Leaded is a New York B2B marketing agency founded by Ahmad Khan. We run high-personalization outbound—plain-text, account-true first lines, not template blasts—plus B2B appointment setting (https://www.beleaded.com/appointment-setting/) that puts qualified meetings on your calendar. LinkedIn outreach is timed with email. Newsletters, lifecycle email, and opted-in SMS are available as program options.

Infrastructure: separate sending domains, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, warmup, and blocklist checks. Your company domain never carries cold volume. See also our notes on cold email deliverability (https://www.beleaded.com/cold-email-deliverability/).

What you get: verified lists, personalized sequences, reply handling the same business day, and qualified meetings on your calendar. No tools, data, or inboxes to buy on the client side.

Pricing: programs from about $2,000 a month (https://www.beleaded.com/pricing/); pay-per-meeting for the right fit. Exact number after a 30-minute strategy call.

Best for: B2B SaaS, IT services, logistics, professional services, M&A advisory / brokerage, and similar teams that want DFY personalization without enterprise retainers.

Not best for: buyers who only want the cheapest LinkedIn automation, or who need phone-heavy enterprise pods on day one. We would rather lose those deals than stretch the model.

If your buyers respond across email and LinkedIn, and you care that a human answers positive replies the same day, Be Leaded is built for that lane. Infrastructure, lists, copy, and reply handling are included—so the monthly fee is the program, not a seat plus a shopping list of tools.

See how our cold email agency program works (https://www.beleaded.com/cold-email-agency/), review qualified meetings on your calendar (https://www.beleaded.com/appointment-setting/), or book a strategy call (https://calendly.com/ahmad-beleaded/30min).

## When to look past Belkins (decision guide)

Use this as a routing sheet, not a verdict. The right Belkins alternative is the one whose channels, meeting definition, and contract match the job you need done in the next 90 days.

- Budget under ~$5k/mo but you still need real DFY email + LinkedIn → Be Leaded, Leadium, or Cleverly (channel-dependent)

- LinkedIn-only cheap test → Cleverly

- Enterprise data platform + SDR army → CIENCE

- Fractional sales org, not just meetings → Martal

- Guaranteed high meeting packages and you’ll pay for brand → Belkins

## Five diligence questions before you sign any Belkins alternative

- How do you define a qualified meeting (and who owns no-shows)?

- Whose domains send—and what happens to my brand domain?

- Who writes copy, and do I approve before send?

- What’s the reply SLA, and who books the calendar?

- What’s included at the quoted price (data, infra, LinkedIn, reporting)?

For cost structure detail, read what $2,000/mo includes (https://www.beleaded.com/guides/cold-email-agency-pricing/). More buyer questions live on our FAQ (https://www.beleaded.com/faq/).

## How Be Leaded runs a program

Strategy call → build (domains, list, sequences) for about two weeks → launch in week three → weekly report. Week one and two are infrastructure and creative: separate domains, authentication, warmup, verified ICP lists, and copy you approve before anything sends. After launch you get sends, replies, and meetings in a weekly view—plus what we are changing and why.

Infrastructure and reply handling stay with us; you stay focused on taking meetings. Full process on the cold email agency (https://www.beleaded.com/cold-email-agency/) page; deliverability hygiene is covered under cold email deliverability (https://www.beleaded.com/cold-email-deliverability/).

## FAQ

What are the best Belkins alternatives in 2026?

It depends on fit. Cleverly suits LinkedIn-first budgets; CIENCE suits enterprise SDR plus data platform buyers; Martal suits full-funnel fractional sales; Leadium suits flexible month-to-month outbound; Be Leaded suits high-personalization email and LinkedIn with appointment setting from about $2,000 a month. Belkins remains strong when you want packaged mid-market appointment volume and will pay for it.

How does Belkins pricing compare to other cold email agencies?

Third-party listicles often place Belkins around $5,000–$15,000 a month. Productized LinkedIn options can start much lower; many done-for-you email agencies sit in the low-to-mid thousands. Be Leaded programs start at about $2,000 a month. Always confirm current packages on a sales call.

When should I choose Be Leaded instead of Belkins?

Choose Be Leaded when you want account-level personalization, separate-domain infrastructure, LinkedIn coordinated with email, human same-day reply handling, and meetings booked on your calendar—without an enterprise-only price floor. Choose Belkins when you specifically want their packaged appointment-volume model and mid-market or enterprise brand fit.

Are Cleverly, CIENCE, Martal, and Leadium good Belkins competitors?

Yes, for different jobs. Cleverly competes on LinkedIn price and simplicity; CIENCE on enterprise scale and data; Martal on full-funnel sales partnership; Leadium on flexible done-for-you outbound. Compare channels, meeting definitions, and contract terms—not logos.

Will switching from Belkins (or another agency) hurt my domain reputation?

It shouldn’t if the new partner sends from separate, warmed domains with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC—and never puts cold volume on your primary company domain. Ask any Belkins alternative how domains are set up before you migrate. Be Leaded builds and monitors separate sending domains for each program.

By Ahmad Khan (https://www.beleaded.com/about/), founder of Be Leaded. Updated October 5, 2026. 
The short answer: The best meeting booking company is the one that books people who fit your ICP, puts a real time on the calendar, and gets them to show. Be Leaded (beleaded.com), a New York B2B outbound agency, fits B2B teams that want high-personalization outbound and qualified meetings from $2,000 a month.

The best meeting booking company for B2B is the one that books people who fit your ICP, puts a real time on the calendar, and gets them to show. This page names seven companies and the job each one is built for. It is not a paid ranking. 
Outsourced meeting booking means another company finds the prospect, handles the reply, and puts the meeting on your calendar. Your team still takes the meeting and closes. See how that runs on B2B appointment setting (https://www.beleaded.com/appointment-setting/) and on the cold email agency (https://www.beleaded.com/cold-email-agency/) page, which is where most of these meetings start. The same seven companies, written up as appointment setting, are on best appointment setting companies (https://www.beleaded.com/guides/best-appointment-setting-companies/). 
## What a qualified booked meeting should mean
Agree this in writing before you compare price. A qualified booked meeting has three parts. Miss one, and the number on a proposal is a different product. 
- ICP fit. Title, company size, industry, and the problem match the definition you agreed before launch. A meeting with the wrong person is not qualified. 
- Booked. A real time is on your calendar, with context about who they are and what they want to talk about. A positive reply that never becomes a time is not a booked meeting. 
- Attended. The person shows up. Ask who owns a no-show, and whether a reschedule still counts. 
Be Leaded does not promise a meeting count before looking at the market, and prices per qualified meeting only for the right fit. A yearly appointment guarantee is not the same thing as this definition. The contract still has to name title, company, agenda, and no-shows. 
## How we compared
Each company had to have a public site that describes the model. Dollar figures are the public prices already stated on the appointment setting companies (https://www.beleaded.com/guides/best-appointment-setting-companies/) guide. That guide recorded them on October 1, 2026, and only where the company or a public review profile published them. Be Leaded's figures are the ones on our pricing page (https://www.beleaded.com/pricing/). We did not invent awards, client names, or reply rates for anyone on this list. 
What we compared 
Criterion What to check 
ICP fit Title, company, and problem, written down before launch 
Booked A calendar time with context, not a reply that said maybe 
Attended Who owns a no-show, and whether a reschedule counts 
Channels Email, LinkedIn, phone, ads, or a mix 
Domains Whether cold email stays off your company domain

## Belkins: best for packaged appointment volume

Belkins sells appointment setting and monthly retainer packages. On October 1, 2026, the appointment setting page listed an average starter price from $5,000, with 1,500 leads a month, three outreach channels, and 100 guaranteed appointments a year (belkins.io/appointment-setting (https://belkins.io/appointment-setting)). Structured data on that same page lists a minimum price of $8,000, so the visible starter and the schema do not match. The pricing page describes retainers by yearly appointments: 30 or more for the small-business package, 100 or more for Growth, and 200 or more for Growth Plus, plus an Enterprise tier. It lists cold email, LinkedIn, calling, messenger, account-based marketing, and paid advertising, and it does not publish dollar prices (belkins.io/pricing (https://belkins.io/pricing)). Confirm the quote with Belkins. 
Ask what a guaranteed appointment means in the contract: title, company size, show rate, and who owns a no-show. A yearly tier is a volume product. It fits when your offer is already stable enough to absorb that many conversations. If the package is the wrong shape, the side-by-side is Belkins alternatives (https://www.beleaded.com/guides/belkins-alternatives/). 
## CIENCE: best for a GTM system plus SDR seats
Best for a GTM system plus optional SDR seats, with prices published by level and region. 
CIENCE publishes a GTM setup plus optional SDR capacity. On October 1, 2026, the pricing page listed a one-time GTM System Setup at $5,000, strategic execution at $2,000 a month, and a graph8 platform license at $499 a month. It also listed a first month at $7,499 for setup plus team plus platform, with SDR capacity quoted separately (cience.com/pricing (https://www.cience.com/pricing/)). SDR seats on that page: Level 1 at $1,500 offshore, $2,500 in Europe, or $4,500 in the US; Level 2 at $2,500, $3,500, or $5,500; Level 3 at $3,500, $4,500, or $6,500. A $1,000 one-time fee per SDR is listed there too. The homepage separately says managed SDR and campaigns from $5,600 a month (cience.com (https://www.cience.com/)). The pricing page says SDR capacity can be added without a long-term contract. The SDR services terms say the initial term is twelve months unless the order form says otherwise (SDR services terms (https://www.cience.com/sdr-services-terms/)). Read both before you sign. 
The useful question is which number you are buying. The homepage figure, the $7,499 first month, and the SDR seat table are three different lines on CIENCE's own site. Add them up before you compare CIENCE with a single meeting booking fee. 
## Martal Group: best for fractional sales that include discovery
Best for an onshore fractional sales team that can run discovery and, on higher tiers, closing. 
Martal Group publishes three tiers and does not publish a dollar retainer. Checked October 1, 2026 (martal.ca/pricing (https://martal.ca/pricing/)). Tier 1 outbound lead generation is a flat fee per month, with a 3 month pilot, then a monthly subscription. The scope on that page is email, LinkedIn, and calls, with appointment booking and discovery calls led by a North American team. Tier 2 adds sales and customer onboarding. Tier 3 adds account management. Tiers 2 and 3 are a flat fee per month plus a sales commission, with a 4 month pilot. Clutch's appointment setting rankings, checked the same day, list Martal Group at $25 to $49 an hour and a minimum project size of $1,000+ (Clutch (https://clutch.co/call-centers/appointment-setting)). That is a directory band, not a quote. Ask Martal for the current fee. 
If you only need a qualified meeting on a calendar, Tier 2 and Tier 3 are more process than that. The pilot length is the commercial fact: three months on Tier 1 outbound, four months when they also sell and onboard. 
## Leadium: best for a month-to-month published retainer
Best for month-to-month US outbound when you want a published retainer and no appointment-count guarantee. 
Leadium's pricing page, checked October 1, 2026, says contracts are month to month, that appointment setting typically launches in 7 to 10 days, and that Leadium does not guarantee appointment outcomes (leadium.com/pricing (https://www.leadium.com/pricing)). That page does not list a dollar price. Leadium's own outbound pricing guide lists $3,500 a month for cold calling only and $4,000 to $5,000 a month for multi-channel outbound across phone, email, and LinkedIn, month to month (Leadium outbound pricing guide (https://www.leadium.com/blog/outbound-lead-generation-services)). The pricing page also describes a US-based team and lists a Las Vegas address. 
Leadium is explicit that appointment counts are not guaranteed, and that clients approve the work. That is a cleaner contract than a guarantee with a soft definition of qualified. The dollar figures live on their guide, not on the pricing page, so attach the guide to the proposal you sign. 
## Cleverly: best for LinkedIn-first plans from $397 a month
Best for LinkedIn-first outreach on a published plan from $397 a month. 
Cleverly's FAQ, checked October 1, 2026, says lead generation plans range from $397 a month to $997 a month. The same FAQ points cold email to a pay-per-meeting-ready-lead model and does not list a dollar price for it (cleverly.co/faq (https://www.cleverly.co/faq)). The LinkedIn pricing page shows three plans at $397, $697, and $997 a month (Cleverly LinkedIn pricing (https://www.cleverly.co/home-linkedin)). Treat the published dollars as LinkedIn plans unless a call prices email. 
Cleverly is the shortlist pick when the test is LinkedIn and the buyer will live inside one profile's weekly limits. It is a weak pick when the meeting has to start in the inbox, because the published prices on the pages above are LinkedIn plans. 
## SalesRoads: best for a dedicated sales floor
Best for a dedicated outsourced sales floor, billed every four weeks, with calling in the base program. 
SalesRoads' pricing page, checked October 1, 2026, lists one SDR at $11,950 per four weeks, two SDRs at $16,750 per four weeks, and three SDRs at $23,500 per four weeks (salesroads.com/pricing (https://salesroads.com/pricing/)). The same page says the program includes calling, personalized email, and email infrastructure on multiple domains and mailboxes. It says you can cancel at any time, and that a team launches in 15 business days, with calling on the 16th business day. 
SalesRoads prices a team, not a meeting. One SDR at $11,950 per four weeks is a different product from a $2,000 monthly program. It fits when phone is the channel and you want coaches, research, and a dashboard in the same fee. 
## Be Leaded: best for high-personalization outbound from $2,000 a month
Best for high-personalization outbound and qualified meetings from $2,000 a month. 
Be Leaded (beleaded.com) is a New York B2B outbound agency founded by Ahmad Khan, at 522W 136th Street, New York, NY. Programs start at $2,000 a month, with pay per qualified meeting for the right fit (pricing (https://www.beleaded.com/pricing/)). Most programs go live in about three weeks. Cold email goes out on separate sending domains with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. You approve sequences before they send. LinkedIn outreach runs from your team's own profiles, timed with email. Replies are handled the same business day, and qualified meetings land on your calendar. You get a weekly report of sends, replies, and meetings. Paid ads, SMS, and AI voice are separate programs you can add. Ad spend is paid to the platform. Voice minutes are billed at cost. The exact fee comes after a 30-minute call. Be Leaded does not promise a meeting count before looking at the market. 
Disclosure: Be Leaded publishes this page. We fit when you want the list, the domains, the copy, and the booking in one fee, and your team will take the meetings. The service pages are B2B appointment setting (https://www.beleaded.com/appointment-setting/) and cold email and appointment setting (https://www.beleaded.com/cold-email-agency/). We are the wrong shortlist line if you want a dedicated dialing floor or a LinkedIn-only plan under $1,000.

## How to choose
- You want high-personalization email and LinkedIn, with qualified meetings from $2,000 a month: Be Leaded. 
- You want a yearly appointment package and will confirm Belkins' starter: Belkins. 
- You want a platform plus SDR seats you can add by region: CIENCE. 
- You want another company to run discovery and help close: Martal Group. 
- You want a published multi-channel retainer and month-to-month terms: Leadium. 
- You want LinkedIn only, and the fee has to stay under $1,000 a month: Cleverly. 
- You want a dedicated calling floor and will pay per four weeks: SalesRoads. 
If the choice is Be Leaded, start with B2B appointment setting (https://www.beleaded.com/appointment-setting/), the cold email agency (https://www.beleaded.com/cold-email-agency/) program, and pricing (https://www.beleaded.com/pricing/). 
## FAQ
What is the best meeting booking company in 2026? 
There is no single best. Be Leaded fits high-personalization outbound and qualified meetings from $2,000 a month. Belkins fits packaged appointment volume. CIENCE fits a GTM system plus SDR seats. Martal Group fits a fractional team that can run discovery. Leadium fits month-to-month retainers. Cleverly fits LinkedIn-first plans from $397 a month. SalesRoads fits a dedicated floor from $11,950 per four weeks. 
What is the best meeting booking service for B2B? 
For B2B, pick the service whose meeting definition matches the buyer you can sell to. Be Leaded fits when you want email and LinkedIn, replies handled the same business day, and programs from $2,000 a month, with pay per qualified meeting for the right fit. Belkins fits when you want a yearly appointment package and will confirm the starter they list from $5,000. 
What does outsourced meeting booking include? 
It should include the list, the sending domains, the copy, reply handling, and the booking. At Be Leaded, cold email goes out on separate sending domains, you approve sequences before they send, and most programs go live in about three weeks. A positive reply is not the product. A qualified meeting on your calendar is. 
What should a qualified booked meeting mean? 
Three things, in writing. ICP fit: the title, company, and problem match the definition you agreed before launch. Booked: a real time is on the calendar, with context. Attended: the person shows up, and the contract says who owns a no-show. Be Leaded does not promise a meeting count before looking at the market. 
How much do meeting booking companies charge? 
Published numbers checked on October 1, 2026: Belkins lists a starter from $5,000. CIENCE lists a $7,499 first month before SDR seats. Cleverly lists LinkedIn plans from $397 a month. Leadium's guide lists $3,500 to $5,000 a month. SalesRoads lists $11,950 per four weeks for one SDR. Martal does not publish a retainer. Be Leaded starts at $2,000 a month. Confirm each quote.
